   180	/-! ## Nonnegativity of the pointwise consistency defect -/
   181	
   182	/-- The off-diagonal outcome sum of two complete measurements placed on
   183	opposite registers is a positive operator.  Formalization-only auxiliary for
   184	blueprint `def:consistency`, paper
   185	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
   186	theorem offDiagonalPlacedProduct_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   187	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   188	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
   189	    (M₁ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
   190	    (M₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)) :
   191	    0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
   192	      if a = b then 0
   193	      else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b) := by
   194	  classical
   195	  have hcomplement : ∀ a : α,
   196	      0 ≤ ∑ b : α, if a = b then (0 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side))
   197	        else M₂.effect b := by
   198	    intro a
   199	    refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => ?_
   200	    by_cases h : a = b
   201	    · rw [if_pos h]
   202	    · rw [if_neg h]
   203	      exact M₂.pos b
   204	  have hrow : ∀ a : α,
   205	      (∑ b : α, if a = b then (0 : Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA
   206	          S.toStrategy.ιB))
   207	        else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)) =
   208	      S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) *
   209	        S.place p₂ (∑ b : α, if a = b then 0 else M₂.effect b) := by
   210	    intro a
   211	    rw [ProjectiveSetting.place_finset_sum_local, Finset.mul_sum]
   212	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   213	    by_cases h : a = b
   214	    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, ProjectiveSetting.place_zero_local, mul_zero]
   215	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]
   216	  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => hrow a]
   217	  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => ?_
   218	  exact ProjectiveSetting.place_mul_place_nonneg S p₁ p₂ hopp (M₁.pos a)
   219	    (hcomplement a)
   220	
   221	/-- The integrand of the consistency defect of two complete measurements placed
   222	on opposite registers is nonnegative.  This is the positivity hypothesis needed
   223	by items 1 and 2 of blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
   224	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
   225	theorem consistencyDefect_integrand_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   226	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   227	    (p₁ p₂ : Placement) (hopp : p₁.IsOpposite p₂)
   228	    (M₁ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
   229	    (M₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)) :
   230	    0 ≤ ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
   231	      if a = b then 0
   232	      else (inner ℂ S.psiHat
   233	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   234	            ℂ).symm
   235	          ((S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)).mulVec
   236	            S.psiHat))).re := by
   237	  classical
   238	  have hform : (∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
   239	        if a = b then 0
   240	        else (inner ℂ S.psiHat
   241	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   242	              ℂ).symm
   243	            ((S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)).mulVec
   244	              S.psiHat))).re) =
   245	      DistanceCalculus.stateQForm S.psiHat
   246	        (∑ a : α, ∑ b : α, if a = b then 0
   247	          else S.place p₁ (M₁.effect a) * S.place p₂ (M₂.effect b)) := by
   248	    rw [DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_finset_sum]
   249	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   250	    rw [DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_finset_sum]
   251	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   252	    by_cases h : a = b
   253	    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, stateQForm_zero_local]
   254	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]
   255	      rfl
   256	  rw [hform]
   257	  exact DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_nonneg S.psiHat
   258	    (offDiagonalPlacedProduct_nonneg S p₁ p₂ hopp M₁ M₂)
   259	
   260	end

   141	theorem avg_restricted_prod_le {P : AdmissibleParams}
   142	    (f : ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) ×
   143	      (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))) -> ℝ)
   144	    (hf : ∀ sample, 0 ≤ f sample) {δ : ℝ}

   146	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   147	        (linePointDist P.toLdParams)) f ≤ δ)
   148	    (kindX kindZ : LineKind) (i j : Fin P.m) :

     4	/-!
     5	# Error inflation of restricted line-point averages
     6	
     7	This module records how a nonnegative average over the line-point distribution
     8	transfers to one restricted component.  The line-point law places weight
     9	`1 / 2` on each of its two kinds and, inside each kind, weight `1 / m` on each
    10	coordinate index, so every restricted component carries mixture weight
    11	`1 / (2 m)` and a nonnegative average inflates by at most `2 m`.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The estimates are items 1 and 2 of blueprint
    16	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, formalizing the unlabelled estimates at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-! ## Averages of the distribution operations -/
    29	
    30	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an average against a dependent bind is the
    31	iterated average.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
    33	theorem avgOver_bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    34	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (f : β → ℝ) :
    35	    avgOver (Distribution.bind μ ν) f =
    36	      avgOver μ (fun a => avgOver (ν a) f) := by
    37	  classical
    38	  unfold avgOver
    39	  have h1 : ∀ b : β, (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) * f b =
    40	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ((ν a).weight b * f b) := by
    41	    intro b
    42	    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    43	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring
    44	  change (∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
    45	    (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) * f b) = _
    46	  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => h1 b, Finset.sum_comm]
    47	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    48	  rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
    49	  congr 1
    50	  refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm
    51	  · intro b hb
    52	    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
    53	  · intro b _ hb
    54	    rw [(ν a).outsideSupport b hb, zero_mul]
    55	
    56	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: an average against a convex mixture is the
    57	convex combination of the two averages.  Blueprint
    58	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1058`. -/
    60	theorem avgOver_mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t)
    61	    (ht1 : t ≤ 1) (μ ν : Distribution α) (f : α → ℝ) :
    62	    avgOver (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν) f =

    65	  unfold avgOver
    66	  have hsplit : (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support,
    67	        (t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a) * f a) =
    68	      t * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a * f a) +
    69	        (1 - t) * (∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a * f a) := by

    71	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => by ring

    73	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * f a := by

    80	    intro a _ ha

    87	iterated average.  Blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
    88	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1056-1058`. -/
    89	theorem avgOver_prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (f : α × β → ℝ) :
    91	    avgOver (Distribution.prod μ ν) f =
    92	      avgOver μ (fun a => avgOver ν (fun b => f (a, b))) := by
    93	  classical

    95	  change (∑ p ∈ μ.support ×ˢ ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2 * f p) = _

    98	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    99	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => by ring

   102	most the whole nonnegative average, scaled by its mixture weight.  Blueprint
   103	`lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1052-1056`. -/
   105	theorem avgOver_bind_uniform_component_le {ι β : Type*}
   106	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] [DecidableEq β]
   107	    (ν : ι → Distribution β) (f : β → ℝ) (hf : ∀ b, 0 ≤ f b) (i : ι) :
   108	    1 / (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) * avgOver (ν i) f ≤
   109	      avgOver (Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution ι) ν) f := by

   125	blueprint `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds`, paper

   104	    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   105	  /-- Every joint point measurement is projective. -/
   106	  projective : ∀ side x z, Measurement.IsProjective (Q side x z)
   107	  /-- Joint point measurements agree across every directed opposite placement. -/
   108	  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   109	    opFamilyDistSq
   110	      (uniformDistribution
   111	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   112	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   113	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   114	      S.psiHat <= δ
   115	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `X`-then-`Z` product. -/
   116	  consistent_XZ : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   117	    opFamilyDistSq
   118	      (uniformDistribution
   119	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   120	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   121	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
   122	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   123	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   124	      S.psiHat <= δ
   125	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product. -/
   126	  consistent_ZX : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   127	    opFamilyDistSq
   128	      (uniformDistribution
   129	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   130	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   131	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
   132	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   133	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))
   134	      S.psiHat <= δ

   136	/-- Joint line measurements and their evaluation consistency from
   137	`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 882--894.  Evaluation uses explicit `Option`
   138	outcomes, including the class of answers not determined at the sampled point. -/
   139	structure CombinedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   140	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   141	    (δ : ℝ) where
   142	  /-- The complete paired-line measurement on each expanded local space. -/
   143	  T : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   144	    LineDesc P.toLdParams -> LineDesc P.toLdParams ->
   145	    Measurement
   146	      (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   147	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   148	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   149	  /-- On an axis-parallel X line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   150	  axis_degree_X : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   151	    lineX.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fX) ->
   152	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   153	  /-- On an axis-parallel Z line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   154	  axis_degree_Z : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   155	    lineZ.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fZ) ->
   156	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   157	  /-- Evaluated line pairs are consistent with the completed point-pair
   158	  measurement on every directed opposite placement. -/
   159	  consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   160	    consistencyDefect
   161	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   162	        (linePointDist P.toLdParams))
   163	      (fun sample answer => S.place p1
   164	        (((T p1.side sample.1.1 sample.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   165	          (evalOpt sample.1.1 sample.1.2 fs.1,
   166	            evalOpt sample.2.1 sample.2.2 fs.2)).effect answer))
   167	      (fun sample answer => S.place p2
   168	        (((points.Q p2.side sample.1.2 sample.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   169	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect answer))
   170	      S.psiHat <= δ

   172	/-! ## The subline distribution -/
   173	
   174	/-- A tuple consisting of an extended line and its projected X and Z lines. -/
   175	abbrev SubLineTriple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   176	  DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
   177	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   178	
   179	/-- An extended line tuple together with a point sampled uniformly on it. -/
   180	abbrev SubLinePointSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   181	  SubLineTriple P ×
   182	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   183	
   184	/-- The shared restricted line kind and two coordinate indices in one mixture
   185	component of the subline law. -/
   186	abbrev SubLineComponent (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   187	  LineKind × (Fin P.m × Fin P.m)
   188	
   189	/-- Select the restricted line-point distribution of a given kind and index. -/
   190	noncomputable def restrictedLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   191	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   192	    Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   193	  match kind with
   194	  | .axis => restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i
   195	  | .diagonal => restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i
   196	
   197	/-- Sample a subline tuple and then a uniform affine parameter on its
   198	extended line. -/
   199	noncomputable def subLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   200	    (D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
   201	    Distribution (SubLinePointSample P) :=
   202	  (Distribution.prod D
   203	    (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map fun sample =>
   204	      (sample.1, sample.1.1.base + sample.2 • sample.1.1.direction)
   205	
   206	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the X projection of an extended point. -/
   207	def subLineXProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   208	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   209	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   210	  (sample.1.2, projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   211	
   212	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the Z projection of an extended point. -/
   213	def subLineZProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   214	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   215	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   216	  (sample.1.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   217	
   218	/-- The X-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   219	noncomputable def subLineXComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   220	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   221	    Distribution
   222	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   223	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   224	  (Distribution.prod
   225	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1)
   226	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2).map Prod.fst)).map
   227	      fun sample => ((sample.1.1, sample.2), sample.1.2)
   228	
   229	/-- The Z-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   230	noncomputable def subLineZComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   231	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   232	    Distribution
   233	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   234	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   235	  (Distribution.prod
   236	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1).map Prod.fst)
   237	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2)).map
   238	      fun sample => ((sample.1, sample.2.1), sample.2.2)
   239	
   240	/-- Directly indexed form of the subline distribution of `lem:qld-sublines`,
   241	paper lines 1063--1069.  Its extended-line marginal is the directly indexed
   242	line-point law rather than the seed-indexed line-point distribution over
   243	`F_q^(2m+2)` of the source statement; that replacement is documented in
   244	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, so this is a
   245	formalization auxiliary record, not the source-labelled statement.  Its
   246	source-mixture field records the X and Z point marginals separately; it does
   247	not assert a joint conditional law for the pair of projected points. -/
   248	structure SubLineWitness (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   249	  /-- The actual distribution of an extended line and two projected lines. -/
   250	  D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)
   251	  /-- The distribution has total mass one. -/
   252	  isProbability : D.IsProbability
   253	  /-- Its extended-line marginal is the direct line-point marginal. -/
   254	  extended_marginal : D.map Prod.fst =
   255	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst
   256	  /-- Every point of an extended line projects onto both stored source lines. -/
   257	  incidence : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, ∀ u ∈ sample.1.pointSet,
   258	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.1.pointSet ∧
   259	      projZ (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.2.pointSet
   260	  /-- Each line triple carries affine data sufficient for
   261	  `combineLinePoly_spec`. -/
   262	  compatibility : ∀ sample ∈ D.support,
   263	    ∃ aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta : PauliScalar P,
   264	      IsCombineLineCompatible
   265	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.base)
   266	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.direction)
   267	        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction
   268	        sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   269	        aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta
   270	  /-- Each one-point projected marginal is a mixture of restricted product
   271	  laws.  No equality for their joint conditional law is claimed. -/
   272	  source_mixture : ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
   273	    components.IsProbability ∧
   274	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineXProjection =
   275	        Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
   276	      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineZProjection =
   277	        Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P)
   278	  /-- An extended axis line has axis-parallel projected lines. -/
   279	  axis_closure : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, sample.1.kind = .axis ->
   280	    sample.2.1.kind = .axis ∧ sample.2.2.kind = .axis
   281	
   282	/-! ## Extended lines and global polynomial pairs -/
   283	
   284	/-- Extended-line POVMs and directly indexed, completed-answer forms of the two
   285	consistency relations in `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034. The direct line
   286	carrier avoids the dimension-divisibility obstruction documented in
   287	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
   288	structure ExtendedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   289	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   290	    (δ : ℝ) where
   291	  /-- The complete extended-line measurement on each player side. -/
   292	  Qline : (side : PlayerSide) -> DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ->
   293	    Measurement (DirectDegPoly P.extendedDirectLd (P.m * P.d + 1))
   294	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   295	  /-- Axis-line outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   296	  axis_degree : ∀ side line f, line.kind = .axis ->
   297	    Not (∀ i, P.d < i.val -> f i = 0) ->
   298	      (Qline side line).effect f = 0
   299	  /-- Alice's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Bob's completed
   300	  combined point measurement. -/
   301	  consistent_alice : consistencyDefect
   302	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   303	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AA'
   304	      (((Qline .alice sample.1).postprocess
   305	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   306	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   307	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BA''
   308	      (((points.Q .bob
   309	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   310	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   311	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   312	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   313	    S.psiHat <= δ
   314	  /-- Bob's evaluated line measurement is consistent with Alice's completed
   315	  combined point measurement. -/
   316	  consistent_bob : consistencyDefect
   317	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd)
   318	    (fun sample answer => S.place .BB'
   319	      (((Qline .bob sample.1).postprocess
   320	        (fun f => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 f).map
   321	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))).effect answer))
   322	    (fun sample answer => S.place .AB''
   323	      (((points.Q .alice
   324	        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   325	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun ab =>
   326	          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * ab.1 +
   327	            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * ab.2)).effect answer))
   328	    S.psiHat <= δ
   329	
   330	/-- The side-indexed global polynomial-pair measurements handed to Chapter 16.
   331	This is the exact conclusion of `lem:qld-4-7`, paper lines 1267--1274, with
   332	the two heterogeneous point-consistency displays stated separately. -/
   333	structure GlobalPairWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
   334	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (δ : ℝ) where
   335	  /-- The complete global polynomial-pair measurement on each player side. -/
   336	  Smeas : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   337	    Measurement (PolyPair P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   338	  /-- Both global polynomial-pair measurements are projective. -/
   339	  projective : ∀ side, Measurement.IsProjective (Smeas side)
   340	  /-- Alice's global evaluations are consistent with Bob's source point
   341	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   342	  point_consistent_alice : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   343	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   344	      (fun u a => S.place .AA'
   345	        (((Smeas .alice).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   346	      (fun u a => S.place .BA''
   347	        ((S.pointMeasExp .bob W u).effect a))
   348	      S.psiHat <= δ
   349	  /-- Bob's global evaluations are consistent with Alice's source point
   350	  measurements, for each Pauli basis. -/
   351	  point_consistent_bob : ∀ W : PauliKind,
   352	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P))
   353	      (fun u a => S.place .BB'
   354	        (((Smeas .bob).postprocess (evalAt W u)).effect a))
   355	      (fun u a => S.place .AB''
   356	        ((S.pointMeasExp .alice W u).effect a))
   357	      S.psiHat <= δ

     4	/-!
     5	# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions
     6	
     7	This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
     8	Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
     9	polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
    10	polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
    11	coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
    12	are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The combining map is blueprint
    17	`def:combine-map`, with paper origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
    19	The restricted laws are blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`,
    20	with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
    33	pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
    34	`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
    35	noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    36	  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)
    37	
    38	/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
    39	measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    40	noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P
    41	
    42	/-- Split the extended coordinate set into the `X` block, the `Z` block, and
    43	the two scalar coordinates.  This is formalization-only coordinate plumbing
    44	for blueprint
    45	`def:combine-map`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    48	    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
    49	  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    50	    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
    51	      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))
    52	
    53	/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    54	def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    55	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))
    56	
    57	/-- Embed a `Z`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    58	def embZ (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    59	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inr i))
    60	
    61	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `alpha`. -/
    62	def alphaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    63	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 0)
    64	
    65	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `beta`. -/
    66	def betaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    67	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 1)
    68	
    69	/-- Project an extended point onto its `X` coordinate block. -/
    70	def projX {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    71	  fun i => u (embX m i)
    72	
    73	/-- Project an extended point onto its `Z` coordinate block. -/
    74	def projZ {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    75	  fun i => u (embZ m i)
    76	
    77	/-- Combine two multivariate polynomials by the formula
    78	`alpha * f(x) + beta * g(z)` from `def:combine-map`.
    79	
    80	Blueprint `def:combine-map`; paper
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
    82	noncomputable def combinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    83	    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * m + 2)) K :=
    84	  MvPolynomial.X (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embX m) f +
    85	    MvPolynomial.X (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embZ m) g
    86	
    87	/-- Evaluation of `combinePoly` is the displayed combining formula. -/
    88	theorem combinePoly_eval {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    89	    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    90	    MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
    91	      u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projX u) f +
    92	        u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projZ u) g := by
    93	  change MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
    94	    u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embX m) f +
    95	      u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embZ m) g
    96	  simp [combinePoly, MvPolynomial.eval_rename]
    97	
    98	/-- A fresh variable times an injectively renamed bounded polynomial retains
    99	the same individual-degree bound.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary for
   100	`def:combine-map`, paper
   101	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
   102	private theorem x_mul_rename_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   103	    {m n d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) {e : Fin m → Fin n} (he : Function.Injective e)
   104	    {a : Fin n} (ha : ∀ i, e i ≠ a) {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K}
   105	    (hp : p ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   106	    MvPolynomial.X a * MvPolynomial.rename e p ∈ polyFunc n K d := by
   107	  classical
   108	  have hrenOutside {j : Fin n} (hj : j ∉ Set.range e) :
   109	      (MvPolynomial.rename e p).degreeOf j = 0 := by
   110	    apply Nat.le_zero.mp
   111	    rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   112	    intro s hs
   113	    rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective he] at hs
   114	    obtain ⟨t, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   115	    simp [Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range _ _ hj]
   116	  have hrenAll (j : Fin n) : (MvPolynomial.rename e p).degreeOf j ≤ d := by
   117	    by_cases hj : j ∈ Set.range e
   118	    · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hj
   119	      rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective he]
   120	      exact degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc hp i
   121	    · rw [hrenOutside hj]
   122	      exact Nat.zero_le d
   123	  have haRange : a ∉ Set.range e := by
   124	    rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
   125	    exact ha i hi
   126	  refine (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree _ _ _).mpr ?_
   127	  intro s hs j
   128	  refine MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp ?_ s hs
   129	  by_cases hj : j = a
   130	  · subst j
   131	    rw [mul_comm]
   132	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_X_self a _).trans (by
   133	      rw [hrenOutside haRange]
   134	      omega)
   135	  · rw [mul_comm, MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_X_of_ne _ hj]
   136	    exact hrenAll j
   137	
   138	/-- The combining polynomial has individual degree at most `d` when
   139	`hd : 1 ≤ d`.  The coordinate blocks are disjoint: `f` depends only on the
   140	`x` variables and `g` only on the `z` variables, so multiplication by `alpha`
   141	or `beta` preserves the degree bound on those old coordinates and gives degree
   142	one only in the corresponding fresh coordinate.  Thus `hd` supplies exactly
   143	the needed bound on the two fresh coordinates; no `d + 1` bound is introduced.
   144	The statement is the well-definedness assertion in
   145	blueprint
   146	`def:combine-map`, with source context
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983` and the
   148	boundary-hypothesis discussion in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   149	-/
   150	theorem combinePoly_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m d : ℕ}
   151	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) {f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K}
   152	    (hf : f ∈ polyFunc m K d) (hg : g ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   153	    combinePoly f g ∈ polyFunc (2 * m + 2) K d := by
   154	  have hsymm : Function.Injective (finCombineEquiv m).symm :=
   155	    (finCombineEquiv m).symm.injective

\section{At a glance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Difficulty: medium.}  Two related matters are recorded.
  First, the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test invokes the

\section{Key theorem forms}

Throughout, $q = 2^r$ with $r$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
theorem forms.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
  \item \textbf{Divisibility-restricted source candidate.}  The source theorem
  form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.  This restriction makes the auxiliary source game defined;
  it does not settle either soundness-import obligation, so this form is not
  established by the present route.
  \item \textbf{Established directly indexed form.}  Quantum
  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; for simultaneity $\kappa$, the error is
  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,\kappa)
  = a(dm'\kappa)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bm'd})$.  This form is proved by
  applying the low individual degree theorem to a combined strategy at
  dimension $M=m'+\kappa$, with sampling count $N=2560000M^3d$, and then
  recovering the $\kappa$ polynomial coordinates.  The proof verifies the low
  individual degree theorem's condition $400Md \le N$; it does not invoke
  Theorem~4.7 of \cite{Ji2021Quantum} or verify that theorem's distinct
  condition $K \ge 12m'(d+1)$.  Thus it avoids rather than discharges the
  two source-import obligations of Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}.
  For $k=1$, transport to the seed-indexed game is established: the two
  mixed relations compress exactly and the global relation is recovered
  from point agreement on the original Hilbert spaces. The general-$k$
  seed-indexed source theorem remains open.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}

We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
proof, and admissibility are at
\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
There, the combined point measurements
$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
individual degree game with parameters
\[
  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
\]
of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.

The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
$\chi(s)$ with
\[
  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
\]
so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.

Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
the instantiation without addressing the divisibility.  Thus even before the
two soundness-import obligations below are considered, this route can apply to
the polynomial-pair lemma only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
\label{sec:import-obligations}

The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.

\paragraph{The cited test.}
In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
lines measurements, and with each other, up to
$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.

\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this
dependence is now retained in a correlated residue register rather than
averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of
the direct-game transport, but it has not been composed with the distinct
pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.
(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
which the test has no counterpart branch.
Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
own value bound.

\paragraph{Obligation 2: the parameter bound.}
Theorem~4.7 requires $K \ge 12 m' t = 12 m' (d+1)$.  The source
instantiates $K = (m')^3 d$, which meets the bound iff
$(m')^2 d \ge 12(d+1)$: this holds for all $d \ge 1$ when $m' \ge 5$,
holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when
$m' \le 3$.  In the game's parameter domain the dimension divides the
admissible field size and is therefore a power of two, so the source's
instantiation violates the hypothesis exactly at $m' \in \{1,2\}$ for
every $d$ and at $m' = 4$ for $d \in \{1,2\}$ --- in particular, in the
multilinear regime $d = 1$, at every dimension $m' \le 4$.  A candidate

    31	/-! ## Conditioning the first factor of a product -/
    32

    42	        (fun w => p w.1), (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w) :
    43	    Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod μ ν) (fun w => p w.1) hpos' =
    44	      Distribution.prod (Distribution.restrict μ p hpos) ν := by
    45	  classical
    46	  have hsupp : (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter (fun w => p w.1) =
    47	      (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support := by
    48	    change (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun w => p w.1) =
    49	      (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support
    50	    ext w
    51	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product]
    52	    tauto
    53	  have hmass : (∑ w ∈ (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter
    54	        (fun w => p w.1), (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w) =
    55	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a := by
    56	    rw [hsupp]
    57	    have h1 : (∑ w ∈ (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support,

    59	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, ∑ b ∈ ν.support,

    64	        (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm,

    73	        ∑ c ∈ (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter (fun w => p w.1),

    76	        ∑ c ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight c else 0) * ν.weight w.2

    81	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h, zero_mul]

    88	    [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    89	    (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
    90	    ∑ w ∈ (uniformDistribution (α × β)).support.filter (fun w => p w.1),

    92	      ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support.filter p,
    93	        (uniformDistribution α).weight a := by
    94	  classical
    95	  rw [Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver,
    96	    Distribution.sum_filter_weight_eq_avgOver,

    99	/-- Conditioning a uniform product law on an event of its first factor leaves

   102	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   110	    Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (α × β)) (fun w => p w.1)
   111	        hpos' =
   112	      Distribution.prod
   113	        (Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution α) p hpos)

     3	/-!

     5	
     6	This module rewrites the two restricted line-point laws of
     7	`def:ith-restricted-line` as push-forwards of a single uniformly sampled
     8	low-degree vector conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber of its retained
     9	scalar seed.  In that form the point block, the seed and the direction block
    10	of the sampled vector are visibly the independent generating data of the
    11	restricted law, which is the description used by the sampling procedure of the
    12	sub-line lemma: there the projected pairs are built either from a direction
    13	block inherited from the extended line or from freshly sampled data, and each
    14	is asserted to follow a restricted law.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The generating descriptions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws themselves are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-! ## Restriction of a push-forward -/
    34	
    35	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restricting a push-forward distribution to a
    36	decidable event is the push-forward of the restriction to the pre-image of
    37	that event.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem Distribution.restrict_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (f : α → β) (p : β → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    41	    (q : α → Prop) [DecidablePred q] (hq : ∀ a, q a ↔ p (f a))
    42	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b)
    43	    (hpos' : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a) :
    44	    Distribution.restrict (μ.map f) p hpos =
    45	      (Distribution.restrict μ q hpos').map f := by
    46	  classical
    47	  have hfiber : ∀ b : β, p b →
    48	      μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    49	        (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b) := by
    50	    intro b hb
    51	    ext a
    52	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    53	    constructor
    54	    · rintro ⟨ha, hab⟩
    55	      exact ⟨⟨ha, (hq a).mpr (hab ▸ hb)⟩, hab⟩
    56	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha, -⟩, hab⟩
    57	      exact ⟨ha, hab⟩
    58	  have himg : (μ.map f).support.filter p = (μ.support.filter q).image f := by
    59	    ext b
    60	    simp only [Distribution.map_support, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_image]
    61	    constructor
    62	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hpb⟩
    63	      exact ⟨a, ⟨ha, (hq a).mpr hpb⟩, rfl⟩
    64	    · rintro ⟨a, ⟨ha1, ha2⟩, rfl⟩
    65	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha1, rfl⟩, (hq a).mp ha2⟩

    67	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a := by

    70	      (s := μ.support.filter q) (t := (μ.support.filter q).image f)

    72	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_

    74	    rw [Distribution.map_weight,
    75	      hfiber _ ((hq a0).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha0).2)]

    77	  · exact himg
    78	  · funext b
    79	    show (if p b then (μ.map f).weight b /
    80	        ∑ c ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight c else 0) =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b),

   112	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
   113	theorem ldSeedEvent_positive (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :

   134	theorem lineDesc_axis_congr {L : LdParams}
   135	    {b b' : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {s : ScalarQ L} (h : b = b')
   136	    (hb : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L s)) b = b)
   137	    (hb' : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L s)) b' = b') :
   138	    LineDesc.axis b s hb = LineDesc.axis b' s hb' := by
   139	  subst h

   147	theorem lineDesc_diagonal_congr {L : LdParams}
   148	    {b b' d d' : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L} {s : ScalarQ L}
   149	    (hb : b = b') (hd : d = d')

   153	    (h2' : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L s).val → d' j = 0) :
   154	    LineDesc.diagonal b s d h1 h2 = LineDesc.diagonal b' s d' h1' h2' := by
   155	  subst hb
   156	  subst hd
   157	  rfl
   158	
   159	/-- The axis-line decoder is unchanged by the axis conditioning map: the
   160	canonical representative of `def:line-representative` is idempotent, so
   161	decoding the conditioned vector and decoding the original vector agree.
   162	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   163	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   164	theorem aLineDescOf_ldALineCL (L : LdParams) (z : LdSpace L) :
   165	    aLineDescOf L (ldALineCL L z) = aLineDescOf L z :=
   166	  lineDesc_axis_congr (lineRepMap_apply_self _ _) _ _
   167	
   168	/-- The diagonal-line decoder is unchanged by the diagonal conditioning map:
   169	the prefix projection and the canonical representative of
   170	`def:line-representative` are both idempotent.  Blueprint
   171	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   172	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   173	theorem dLineDescOf_ldDLineCL (L : LdParams) (z : LdSpace L) :
   174	    dLineDescOf L (ldDLineCL L z) = dLineDescOf L z := by
   175	  have hdir : prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed (ldDLineCL L z)))
   176	        (LdSpace.direction (ldDLineCL L z))
   177	      = prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)) (LdSpace.direction z) :=
   178	    prefixProjection_idempotent _ _
   179	  have hpt : lineRepMap
   180	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed (ldDLineCL L z)))
   181	          (LdSpace.direction (ldDLineCL L z)))
   182	        (LdSpace.point (ldDLineCL L z))
   183	      = lineRepMap
   184	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)) (LdSpace.direction z))
   185	        (LdSpace.point z) := by
   186	    rw [hdir]
   187	    exact lineRepMap_apply_self _ _
   188	  exact lineDesc_diagonal_congr hpt hdir _ _ _ _
   189	
   190	/-! ## Generating laws of the restricted line-point distributions -/
   191	
   192	/-- The `i`-th restricted axis-line law is the law of the pair consisting of
   193	the canonical axis-parallel line through a low-degree vector and its point
   194	block, when that vector is uniform conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber
   195	of its seed.  This is the generating description used in the sampling
   196	procedure of blueprint
   197	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   199	theorem restrictedALineDist_eq_map_restrict (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   200	    restrictedALineDist L i =
   201	      (Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L))
   202	          (ldSeedEvent L i) (ldSeedEvent_positive L i)).map
   203	        (fun z => (aLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z)) := by
   204	  classical
   205	  have hcomp :
   206	      (fun z : LdSpace L =>
   207	          (aLineDescOf L (ldALineCL L z), LdSpace.point (ldPointCL L z))) =
   208	        fun z : LdSpace L => (aLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z) := by
   209	    funext z
   210	    rw [aLineDescOf_ldALineCL]
   211	    rfl
   212	  unfold restrictedALineDist restrictedALinePreDist clDistribution
   213	  rw [Distribution.restrict_map (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L))
   214	      (fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z))
   215	      (restrictedLineSeedEvent L i) (ldSeedEvent L i) (fun _ => Iff.rfl)
   216	      _ (ldSeedEvent_positive L i),
   217	    Distribution.map_map]
   218	  exact congrArg _ hcomp
   219	
   220	/-- The `i`-th restricted diagonal-line law is the law of the pair consisting
   221	of the canonical diagonal line through a low-degree vector and its point
   222	block, when that vector is uniform conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber
   223	of its seed.  This is the generating description used in the sampling
   224	procedure of blueprint
   225	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   226	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   227	theorem restrictedDLineDist_eq_map_restrict (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   228	    restrictedDLineDist L i =
   229	      (Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L))
   230	          (ldSeedEvent L i) (ldSeedEvent_positive L i)).map
   231	        (fun z => (dLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z)) := by
   232	  classical
   233	  have hcomp :
   234	      (fun z : LdSpace L =>
   235	          (dLineDescOf L (ldDLineCL L z), LdSpace.point (ldPointCL L z))) =
   236	        fun z : LdSpace L => (dLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z) := by
   237	    funext z
   238	    rw [dLineDescOf_ldDLineCL]
   239	    rfl
   240	  unfold restrictedDLineDist restrictedDLinePreDist clDistribution
   241	  rw [Distribution.restrict_map (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L))
   242	      (fun z => (ldDLineCL L z, ldPointCL L z))
   243	      (restrictedLineSeedEvent L i) (ldSeedEvent L i) (fun _ => Iff.rfl)
   244	      _ (ldSeedEvent_positive L i),
   245	    Distribution.map_map]
   246	  exact congrArg _ hcomp
   247	
   248	end

     3	/-!
     4	# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
     5	
     6	The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
     7	the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
     8	scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
     9	coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
    10	of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
    11	This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
    12	source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
    13	reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
    14	line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
    15	same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    20	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    21	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    22	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    23	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	open scoped BigOperators
    27	
    28	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    29	
    30	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-! ## The identification of the two scalar fields as a bijection -/
    35	
    36	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    37	source scalar field on one source block, presented as a bijection.  Blueprint
    38	`def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	noncomputable def directBlockToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    41	    (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃ (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) where
    42	  toFun v := fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v i)
    43	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    44	  left_inv v := by
    45	    funext i
    46	    simp
    47	  right_inv v := by
    48	    funext i
    49	    simp
    50	
    51	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    52	source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
    53	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    55	noncomputable def directPointToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    56	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    57	      (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) where
    58	  toFun := directPointToPauli P
    59	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    60	  left_inv v := by
    61	    funext i
    62	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    63	  right_inv v := by
    64	    funext i
    65	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    66	
    67	/-- The `X` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `X`
    68	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	theorem projX_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    72	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projX u) := rfl
    73	
    74	/-- The `Z` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `Z`
    75	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    77	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    78	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    79	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projZ u) := rfl
    80	
    81	/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
    82	
    83	/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field
    84	is uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    85	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    86	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (uniformDistribution
    88	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    89	        (directPointToPauli P) =
    90	      uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) :=
    91	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directPointToPauliEquiv P)
    92	
    93	/-- A uniformly random source block transported to the source scalar field is
    94	uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    96	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directBlockToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    97	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    98	        (fun v => directBlockToPauliEquiv P v) =
    99	      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :=
   100	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   101	
   102	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly random extended point, read in the
   103	source scalar field, are independent and uniformly random.  Blueprint
   104	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   106	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   107	    (uniformDistribution
   108	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   109	        (fun u => (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   110	          projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   111	      Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   112	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   113	  classical
   114	  have hfun :
   115	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   116	          (projX (directPointToPauli P u), projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   117	        fun u => (Equiv.prodCongr (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   118	          (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)) (projX u, projZ u) := rfl
   119	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)),
   120	    uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ, ← uniformDistribution_prod,
   121	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv, uniformDistribution_prod]
   122	
   123	/-! ## Resampling a uniform point along a line -/
   124	
   125	/-- Reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on
   126	the line through the canonical representative, in a fixed direction, of a
   127	uniformly random point is the same as reading that function at a uniformly
   128	random point.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   130	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul_comp {K : Type*} [Field K]
   131	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} {γ : Type*} [DecidableEq γ]
   132	    (v : Fin m → K) (g : (Fin m → K) → γ) :
   133	    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K))
   134	          (uniformDistribution K)).map
   135	        (fun w => g (lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v)) =
   136	      (uniformDistribution (Fin m → K)).map g := by
   137	  classical
   138	  rw [← uniformDistribution_prod,
   139	    ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun w : (Fin m → K) × K =>
   140	      lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) g,
   141	    uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul]
   142	
   143	end
   144	
   145	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     4	/-!
     5	# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
     6	
     7	This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
     8	the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
     9	is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
    10	coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
    11	the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
    12	point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
    13	commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
    14	canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
    15	field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
    16	the same three coordinate ranges.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    21	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    23	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    24	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open scoped BigOperators
    28	
    29	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    30	
    31	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    32	
    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	/-! ## Linearity of the coordinate blocks -/
    36	
    37	/-- The `X` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    38	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	theorem projX_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    41	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    42	    projX (u + v) = projX u + projX v := rfl
    43	
    44	/-- The `Z` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    45	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	theorem projZ_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    48	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    49	    projZ (u + v) = projZ u + projZ v := rfl
    50	
    51	/-- The `X` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    52	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    54	theorem projX_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    55	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    56	    projX (t • u) = t • projX u := rfl
    57	
    58	/-- The `Z` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    59	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    61	theorem projZ_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    62	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    63	    projZ (t • u) = t • projZ u := rfl
    64	
    65	/-! ## The coordinate blocks of an extended point -/
    66	
    67	/-- Split an extended point into its two source point blocks and its two
    68	scalar coordinates.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	def extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    71	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    72	      ((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    73	          (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
    74	        (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :=
    75	  (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCombineEquiv P.m)
    76	      (Equiv.refl (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).trans
    77	    ((Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _).trans
    78	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.refl _)))
    79	
    80	/-- The first block of the decomposition is the `X` block. -/
    81	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX (P : AdmissibleParams)
    82	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    83	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.1 = projX u := by
    84	  funext i
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- The second block of the decomposition is the `Z` block. -/
    88	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams)
    89	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    90	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.2 = projZ u := by
    91	  funext i
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The first scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `alpha`. -/
    95	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_alpha (P : AdmissibleParams)
    96	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    97	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 0 = u (alphaVar P.m) := rfl
    98	
    99	/-- The second scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `beta`. -/
   100	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_beta (P : AdmissibleParams)
   101	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   102	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 1 = u (betaVar P.m) := rfl
   103	
   104	/-- The block decomposition of an extended point carries the uniform law to
   105	the uniform law.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	theorem uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   108	    (uniformDistribution
   109	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   110	        (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) =
   111	      uniformDistribution
   112	        (((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
   113	            (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
   114	          (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) :=
   115	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   116	
   117	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly sampled extended point are
   118	independent and uniform.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   120	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   121	    (uniformDistribution
   122	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   123	        (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)) =
   124	      Distribution.prod
   125	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   126	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) := by
   127	  have hfun :
   128	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   129	          (projX u, projZ u)) =
   130	        fun u => (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1 := by
   131	    funext u
   132	    rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   133	    exact ⟨(extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX P u).symm,
   134	      (extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ P u).symm⟩
   135	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) Prod.fst,
   136	    uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv,
   137	    uniformDistribution_map_fst, uniformDistribution_prod]
   138	
   139	/-! ## Transport to the source scalar field -/
   140	
   141	/-- The `X` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   142	is the transport of its `X` block.  Blueprint
   143	`def:combine-map`, paper
   144	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   145	theorem projX_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   146	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   147	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) =
   148	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projX u i) := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- The `Z` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   151	is the transport of its `Z` block.  Blueprint
   152	`def:combine-map`, paper
   153	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   154	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   155	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   156	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) =
   157	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projZ u i) := rfl
   158	
   159	/-! ## The blocks of an extended direct sample -/
   160	
   161	/-- The stored index, point block and direction block of a uniformly sampled
   162	direct low-degree vector are independent and uniform.  Blueprint
   163	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   165	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   166	    (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map (directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D) =
   167	      uniformDistribution
   168	        (Fin D.m ×
   169	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))) :=
   170	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   171	
   172	/-! ## Compatibility data read off the coordinate blocks -/
   173	
   174	/-- An extended line is compatible with two source lines as soon as each of
   175	its two point blocks is an affine reparameterization of the corresponding
   176	source line: the base block is a point of the source line and the direction
   177	block is a multiple of the source direction.  The two scalar coordinates of
   178	the compatibility data are the `alpha` and `beta` coordinates of the extended
   179	base and direction.  This supplies the domain condition preceding Equation
   180	`eq:combine-lines` in blueprint
   181	`def:combine-map`, paper
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   183	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   184	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K) (aX bX aZ bZ : K)
   185	    (hX : projX u = uX + aX • vX) (hXv : projX v = bX • vX)
