     3	/-!
     4	# Reshuffling products of finitely supported laws
     5	
     6	The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma produces its six independent
     7	generating blocks in one grouping, while the restricted line-point laws that
     8	the projected marginals must match present the same six blocks in another
     9	grouping.  This module records the rewriting rules that pass between two such
    10	presentations: the support and the weight of a product, the fact that a
    11	push-forward along a bijection is determined by the supports and weights it
    12	compares, and the push-forward of the second factor of a product.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    17	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    19	The product operation is that of blueprint
    20	`def:line-point-dist`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-! ## The support and the weight of a product -/
    32	
    33	/-- The support of a product law is the product of the supports.  Blueprint
    34	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    36	-/
    37	theorem Distribution.prod_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    38	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) :
    39	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).support = μ.support ×ˢ ν.support := rfl
    40	
    41	/-- The weight of a product law is the product of the weights.  Blueprint
    42	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    44	-/
    45	theorem Distribution.prod_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    46	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (w : α × β) :
    47	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w = μ.weight w.1 * ν.weight w.2 := rfl
    48	
    49	/-! ## Push-forward along a bijection -/
    50	
    51	/-- A push-forward along a bijection is identified by the supports and the
    52	weights it compares: if the map matches the two supports and carries each
    53	weight to the corresponding weight, and if it has a two-sided inverse, the
    54	push-forward is the target law.  Blueprint
    55	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    57	theorem Distribution.map_bijective_eq {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    58	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (f : α → β)
    59	    (g : β → α) (hgf : ∀ a, g (f a) = a) (hfg : ∀ b, f (g b) = b)
    60	    (hs : ∀ a, a ∈ μ.support ↔ f a ∈ ν.support)
    61	    (hw : ∀ a, μ.weight a = ν.weight (f a)) :
    62	    μ.map f = ν := by
    63	  classical
    64	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    65	  · rw [Distribution.map_support]
    66	    ext b
    67	    simp only [Finset.mem_image]
    68	    constructor
    69	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    70	      exact (hs a).mp ha
    71	    · intro hb
    72	      refine ⟨g b, (hs (g b)).mpr ?_, hfg b⟩
    73	      rw [hfg b]
    74	      exact hb
    75	  · funext b
    76	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    77	    have hfilter : μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    78	        μ.support.filter (fun a => a = g b) := by
    79	      ext a
    80	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    81	      constructor
    82	      · rintro ⟨ha, h⟩
    83	        exact ⟨ha, by rw [← h, hgf]⟩
    84	      · rintro ⟨ha, h⟩
    85	        exact ⟨ha, by rw [h, hfg]⟩
    86	    rw [hfilter, Finset.filter_eq' μ.support (g b)]
    87	    by_cases hmem : g b ∈ μ.support
    88	    · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton, hw (g b), hfg]
    89	    · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty]
    90	      refine (ν.outsideSupport b ?_).symm
    91	      intro hb
    92	      exact hmem ((hs (g b)).mpr (by rw [hfg b]; exact hb))
    93	
    94	/-! ## Push-forward of the second factor of a product -/
    95	
    96	/-- Pushing the second factor of a product forward is pushing the product
    97	forward along the map acting on that factor alone.  Blueprint
    98	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	theorem Distribution.prod_map_right {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   101	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
   102	    (g : β → γ) :
   103	    Distribution.prod μ (ν.map g) =
   104	      (Distribution.prod μ ν).map (fun w => (w.1, g w.2)) := by
   105	  classical
   106	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   107	  · change μ.support ×ˢ (ν.support.image g) =
   108	      (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).image (fun w => (w.1, g w.2))
   109	    ext w
   110	    obtain ⟨x, c⟩ := w
   111	    simp only [Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_image, Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.exists]
   112	    constructor
   113	    · rintro ⟨hx, b, hb, rfl⟩
   114	      exact ⟨x, b, ⟨hx, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
   115	    · rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
   116	      exact ⟨ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
   117	  · funext w
   118	    obtain ⟨x, c⟩ := w
   119	    have hfilter :
   120	        (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (p.1, g p.2) = (x, c)) =
   121	          (μ.support.filter (fun a => a = x)) ×ˢ
   122	            (ν.support.filter (fun b => g b = c)) := by
   123	      ext p
   124	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Prod.mk.injEq]
   125	      tauto
   126	    have hx : ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter (fun a => a = x), μ.weight a =
   127	        μ.weight x := by
   128	      rw [Finset.filter_eq' μ.support x]
   129	      by_cases hmem : x ∈ μ.support
   130	      · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton]
   131	      · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty, μ.outsideSupport x hmem]
   132	    change μ.weight x * (ν.map g).weight c =
   133	      ∑ p ∈ (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (p.1, g p.2) = (x, c)),
   134	        μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
   135	    rw [hfilter, Finset.sum_product,
   136	      Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun a _ =>
   137	        (Finset.mul_sum (ν.support.filter (fun b => g b = c))
   138	          (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm),
   139	      ← Finset.sum_mul, hx]
   140	    rfl
   141	
   142	end
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Rewriting rules for dependent mixtures of finite distributions
     5	
     6	This module records the elementary rewriting rules for the dependent mixture
     7	of finite distributions that the sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
     8	uses: a mixture indexed along a push-forward is the mixture indexed along the
     9	original law, iterated mixtures associate, a mixture is unchanged when the
    10	mixed family is changed only outside the index support, a mixture of a
    11	constant family is that constant, a product with a fixed independent factor
    12	distributes over a mixture, and an equal two-term mixture is the mixture
    13	indexed by a uniform pair of labels.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    18	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    20	The mixture, product and equal-mixture operations are those of
    21	blueprint `def:line-point-dist`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    27	
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-! ## Reindexing a dependent mixture -/
    33	
    34	/-- Mixing along a push-forward index is mixing along the original index.
    35	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    37	theorem Distribution.bind_map_left {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    38	    [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (f : α → β) (ν : β → Distribution γ) :
    39	    Distribution.bind (μ.map f) ν =
    40	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => ν (f a)) := by
    41	  classical
    42	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    43	  · change (μ.support.image f).biUnion (fun b => (ν b).support) =
    44	      μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν (f a)).support)
    45	    ext c
    46	    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_image]
    47	    constructor
    48	    · rintro ⟨b, ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hc⟩
    49	      exact ⟨a, ha, hc⟩
    50	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, hc⟩
    51	      exact ⟨f a, ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hc⟩
    52	  · funext c
    53	    change (∑ b ∈ μ.support.image f, (μ.map f).weight b * (ν b).weight c) =
    54	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν (f a)).weight c
    55	    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    56	      (s := μ.support) (t := μ.support.image f) (g := f)
    57	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image_of_mem f ha)
    58	      (fun a => μ.weight a * (ν (f a)).weight c)]
    59	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    60	    rw [Distribution.map_weight, Finset.sum_mul]
    61	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    62	    rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
    63	
    64	/-- A dependent mixture depends on the mixed family only on the index
    65	support.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    67	theorem Distribution.bind_congr_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν ν' : α → Distribution β)
    69	    (h : ∀ a ∈ μ.support, ν a = ν' a) :
    70	    Distribution.bind μ ν = Distribution.bind μ ν' := by
    71	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    72	  · change μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support) =
    73	      μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν' a).support)
    74	    exact Finset.biUnion_congr rfl fun a ha => by rw [h a ha]
    75	  · funext b
    76	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => by rw [h a ha]
    77	
    78	/-- A dependent mixture of a constant family is that constant law.  Blueprint
    79	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    81	theorem Distribution.bind_const {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    82	    (μ : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (ν : Distribution β) :
    83	    Distribution.bind μ (fun _ => ν) = ν := by
    84	  have hne : μ.support.Nonempty := by
    85	    rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    86	    by_contra hcard
    87	    have hempty : μ.support = ∅ := by
    88	      rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero]
    89	      omega
    90	    have h1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
    91	    rw [hempty] at h1
    92	    simp at h1
    93	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    94	  · change μ.support.biUnion (fun _ => ν.support) = ν.support
    95	    ext b
    96	    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion]
    97	    constructor
    98	    · rintro ⟨a, -, hb⟩
    99	      exact hb
   100	    · intro hb
   101	      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
   102	      exact ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
   103	  · funext b
   104	    change (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b) = ν.weight b
   105	    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hμ.weight_sum_eq_one, one_mul]
   106	
   107	/-! ## Associativity of dependent mixtures -/
   108	
   109	/-- Iterated dependent mixtures associate.  Blueprint
   110	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   112	theorem Distribution.bind_bind {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   113	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (ρ : β → Distribution γ) :
   114	    Distribution.bind (Distribution.bind μ ν) ρ =
   115	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => Distribution.bind (ν a) ρ) := by
   116	  classical
   117	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   118	  · change (μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)).biUnion
   119	        (fun b => (ρ b).support) =
   120	      μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support.biUnion (fun b => (ρ b).support))
   121	    ext c
   122	    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion]
   123	    constructor
   124	    · rintro ⟨b, ⟨a, ha, hb⟩, hc⟩
   125	      exact ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hc⟩
   126	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hc⟩
   127	      exact ⟨b, ⟨a, ha, hb⟩, hc⟩
   128	  · funext c
   129	    change (∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   130	        (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) * (ρ b).weight c) =
   131	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a *
   132	        ∑ b ∈ (ν a).support, (ν a).weight b * (ρ b).weight c
   133	    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ =>
   134	      Finset.sum_mul μ.support (fun a => μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b)
   135	        ((ρ b).weight c), Finset.sum_comm]
   136	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
   137	    have hsub : (ν a).support ⊆ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support) :=
   138	      fun b hb => Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
   139	    have hzero : ∀ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
   140	        b ∉ (ν a).support →
   141	        μ.weight a * ((ν a).weight b * (ρ b).weight c) = 0 := by
   142	      intro b _ hbnot
   143	      rw [(ν a).outsideSupport b hbnot, zero_mul, mul_zero]
   144	    rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_subset hsub hzero]
   145	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => mul_assoc _ _ _
   146	
   147	/-! ## Products with an independent factor -/
   148	
   149	/-- A product with a fixed independent second factor distributes over a
   150	dependent mixture of the first factor.  Blueprint
   151	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   153	theorem Distribution.prod_bind_left {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   154	    [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β)
   155	    (ρ : Distribution γ) :
   156	    Distribution.prod (Distribution.bind μ ν) ρ =
   157	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => Distribution.prod (ν a) ρ) := by
   158	  classical
   159	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   160	  · change (μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)) ×ˢ ρ.support =
   161	      μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support ×ˢ ρ.support)
   162	    ext w
   163	    simp only [Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_biUnion]
   164	    constructor
   165	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, hb⟩, hc⟩
   166	      exact ⟨a, ha, hb, hc⟩
   167	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, hb, hc⟩
   168	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha, hb⟩, hc⟩
   169	  · funext w
   170	    change (∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight w.1) * ρ.weight w.2 =
   171	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ((ν a).weight w.1 * ρ.weight w.2)
   172	    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   173	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => mul_assoc _ _ _
   174	
   175	/-! ## The equal two-term mixture as a uniform dependent mixture -/
   176	
   177	/-- The equal mixture of two laws is the dependent mixture indexed by a
   178	uniform pair of labels.  Blueprint `def:line-point-dist`, paper
   179	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
   180	-/
   181	theorem Distribution.bind_uniform_fin_two {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   182	    (μ ν : Distribution α) :
   183	    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2)) ![μ, ν] =
   184	      Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num) μ ν := by
   185	  classical
   186	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   187	  · change (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2)).biUnion
   188	        (fun i => (![μ, ν] i).support) = μ.support ∪ ν.support
   189	    ext a
   190	    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_union]
   191	    constructor
   192	    · rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
   193	      fin_cases i
   194	      · exact Or.inl hi
   195	      · exact Or.inr hi
   196	    · rintro (h | h)
   197	      · exact ⟨0, h⟩
   198	      · exact ⟨1, h⟩
   199	  · funext a
   200	    change (∑ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2)),
   201	        (uniformDistribution (Fin 2)).weight i * (![μ, ν] i).weight a) =
   202	      1 / 2 * μ.weight a + (1 - 1 / 2) * ν.weight a
   203	    rw [Fin.sum_univ_two, uniformDistribution_weight_apply,
   204	      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Fintype.card_fin]
   205	    norm_num
   206	
   207	end
   208	
   209	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Uniform points of a line and the blocks of a coordinate direction
     5	
     6	This module records the two elementary geometric inputs of the sampling
     7	procedure of the sub-line lemma.  First, a uniformly random point of the
     8	coordinate space is the same thing as a uniformly random canonical
     9	representative together with a uniformly random affine parameter along the
    10	direction: the map sending a pair to the point at that parameter on the line
    11	through the representative has constant fibers of size `q`, because the
    12	kernel of the canonical representative map is the span of the direction and
    13	for the zero direction that map is the identity.  Second, the two coordinate
    14	blocks of an elementary coordinate direction of the extended space are the
    15	corresponding elementary direction of the source space in the block that
    16	carries the coordinate, and zero in the other block and at the two scalar
    17	coordinates.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The two statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    22	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    24	The canonical representative map is blueprint
    25	`def:line-representative`; the coordinate blocks are those of
    26	blueprint `def:combine-map`.
    27	-/
    28	
    29	open scoped BigOperators
    30	
    31	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    32	
    33	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    34	
    35	noncomputable section
    36	
    37	/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
    38	
    39	/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
    40	`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
    41	is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
    42	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    43	-/
    44	theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    45	    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
    46	  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
    47	  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
    48	  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
    49	  exact h.symm
    50	
    51	/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
    52	
    53	/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
    54	canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
    55	the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
    56	`q` elements: for a nonzero direction the parameter is determined and the
    57	representative varies over a coset of the span of the direction, and for the

    65	      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
    66	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card K) fun x => ?_

    68	  · subst hv
    69	    have hfilter :
    70	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    71	            fun w => lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) w.1 + w.2 • (0 : Fin m → K)
    72	              = x)

    74	      ext w
    75	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
    76	        Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton, and_true, smul_zero,
    77	        add_zero, lineRepMap_zero_apply]

    80	  · have hinj : Function.Injective
    81	        (fun c : K => (lineRepMap v x + c • v, directLineRepParameter v x)) := by

    83	      have hc' : c₁ • v = c₂ • v := by
    84	        have h := congrArg Prod.fst hc

    92	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    93	            fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v = x)

    96	                directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    97	      ext w
    98	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image]
    99	      constructor
   100	      · intro hw
   101	        have hrep : lineRepMap v w.1 = lineRepMap v x := by
   102	          rw [← hw, lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]

   104	          rw [← hrep]
   105	          exact hw.symm

   113	          abel
   114	        rw [Prod.ext_iff]

   116	      · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
   117	        show lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v x + c • v) +
   118	          directLineRepParameter v x • v = x
   119	        rw [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]

     4	/-!
     5	# The projected marginals of the sub-line law
     6	
     7	This module identifies the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law
     8	of `lem:qld-sublines` as mixtures of the restricted product laws.  The two
     9	source lines of a sampled triple depend on the drawn extended point only
    10	through the canonical representatives of its two source blocks, and those
    11	representatives are unchanged when the drawn point is replaced by any point of
    12	the extended line; a uniform point of the extended line through a uniform
    13	point is a uniform point, so the drawn point may be replaced throughout by the
    14	point that is finally retained.  The six generating blocks of the resulting
    15	law -- the two source point blocks, the two scalar seeds and the two source
    16	direction blocks -- are then regrouped into the two restricted product laws
    17	carried by the two indices of the branch.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The identification is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    22	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    24	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    25	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    26	-/

    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    33	
    34	noncomputable section

    48	      lineRepMap
    49	        (subLineSourceDirection P kind (chiIndex P.toLdParams s) d) b') :
    50	    subLineSourceLine P kind b s d = subLineSourceLine P kind b' s d := by

    53	  · exact lineDesc_diagonal_congr h rfl _ _ _ _

   478	            (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.2)) w.1.2.2
   479	            (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.1))),
   480	        (projX (directPointToPauli P w.2),
   481	          projZ (directPointToPauli P w.2))))).symm ?_
   482	    refine Eq.trans hpp2 ?_
   483	    rw [← hfinal]
   484	    exact (Distribution.map_map _
   485	      (fun w : ((((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) ×
   486	            (ScalarQ P.toLdParams × ScalarQ P.toLdParams)) ×
   487	          ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) =>
   488	        ((w.2.1, (w.1.2.1, w.1.1.1)), (w.2.2, (w.1.2.2, w.1.1.2))))
   489	      (fun w => ((subLineSourceLine P kind w.1.1 w.1.2.1 w.1.2.2,
   490	          subLineSourceLine P kind w.2.1 w.2.2.1 w.2.2.2),
   491	        (w.1.1, w.2.1)))).symm
   492	
   493	/-! ## The two one-point projected marginals of one branch -/
   494	
   495	/-- At a fixed line kind and a fixed extended coordinate, the joint law of the
   496	two source lines of a sampled triple together with the source `X` block of a
   497	uniform point of its extended line is the `X` component law of the two indices
   498	of that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   499	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   500	theorem subLineBranchRaw_map_projX (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   501	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
   502	    (Distribution.prod
   503	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   504	          (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   505	            (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k))))
   506	        (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map
   507	      (fun p => ((subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).2,
   508	        projX (directPointToPauli P
   509	          ((subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).1.base +
   510	            p.2 • (subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).1.direction)))) =
   511	      subLineXComponentDist P
   512	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
   513	  classical
   514	  have h := congrArg
   515	    (fun D : Distribution ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   516	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) =>
   517	      Distribution.map D (fun z => (z.1, z.2.1)))
   518	    (subLineBranchRaw_map_joint P kind k)

   520	  refine Eq.trans h ?_
   521	  exact (subLineXComponentDist_eq_map_prod P kind (subLineXIndex P k)
   522	    (subLineZIndex P k)).symm

   525	two source lines of a sampled triple together with the source `Z` block of a
   526	uniform point of its extended line is the `Z` component law of the two indices
   527	of that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   528	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   529	theorem subLineBranchRaw_map_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   530	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
   531	    (Distribution.prod
   532	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   533	          (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   534	            (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k))))
   535	        (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map
   536	      (fun p => ((subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).2,
   537	        projZ (directPointToPauli P
   538	          ((subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).1.base +
   539	            p.2 • (subLineTripleOf P kind k p.1).1.direction)))) =
   540	      subLineZComponentDist P
   541	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
   542	  classical
   543	  have h := congrArg
   544	    (fun D : Distribution ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   545	        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) =>
   546	      Distribution.map D (fun z => (z.1, z.2.2)))
   547	    (subLineBranchRaw_map_joint P kind k)

   549	  refine Eq.trans h ?_
   550	  exact (subLineZComponentDist_eq_map_prod P kind (subLineXIndex P k)
   551	    (subLineZIndex P k)).symm

     3	/-!
     4	# The projected mixtures of the sub-line law
     5	
     6	This module assembles the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law of
     7	`lem:qld-sublines` into mixtures of the restricted product laws.  Drawing a
     8	uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line laws is the same
     9	mixture of the corresponding uniform-point laws, so the two projected
    10	marginals of the sub-line law are the mixtures, over the drawn kind and the
    11	drawn extended coordinate, of the projected marginals of one branch at one
    12	extended coordinate.  Each of those is the component law of the pair of
    13	indices carried by that branch, so the mixing law is the law of the kind
    14	together with the pair of indices assigned to a uniform extended coordinate.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The assembly is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-! ## The uniform point of a mixture of line laws -/
    34	
    35	/-- Drawing a uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line-triple
    36	laws is the corresponding mixture of the uniform-point laws.  Blueprint
    37	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem subLinePointDist_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) {α : Type*}
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
    41	    subLinePointDist P (Distribution.bind μ ν) =
    42	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => subLinePointDist P (ν a)) := by
    43	  classical
    44	  unfold subLinePointDist
    45	  rw [Distribution.prod_bind_left, Distribution.bind_map]
    46	
    47	/-! ## The projected marginals of one branch at one extended coordinate -/
    48	
    49	/-- One branch of the sampling procedure, read at a fixed extended coordinate,
    50	is the law of the triple decoded from the auxiliary randomness of that
    51	coordinate.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	theorem subLineBranchDist_eq_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
    54	    subLineBranchDist P kind =
    55	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
    56	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    57	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    58	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    59	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w := by
    60	  classical
    61	  rw [subLineBranchDist, subLineRawDist, Distribution.bind_map]
    62	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
    63	  rw [Distribution.map_map]
    64	
    65	/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
    66	one extended coordinate is the `X` component law of the pair of indices of
    67	that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    69	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    70	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    71	    (subLinePointDist P
    72	        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    73	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    74	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    75	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineXProjection =
    76	      subLineXComponentDist P
    77	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
    78	  classical
    79	  unfold subLinePointDist
    80	  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    81	  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projX P kind k
    82	
    83	/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
    84	one extended coordinate is the `Z` component law of the pair of indices of
    85	that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    87	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    88	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    89	    (subLinePointDist P
    90	        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    91	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    92	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    93	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineZProjection =
    94	      subLineZComponentDist P
    95	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
    96	  classical
    97	  unfold subLinePointDist
    98	  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    99	  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projZ P kind k
   100	
   101	/-! ## The mixing law of the two indices -/
   102	
   103	/-- The law of the kind and the pair of source indices assigned to a uniform
   104	extended coordinate of one branch.  Blueprint
   105	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	noncomputable def subLineComponentBranch (P : AdmissibleParams)
   108	    (kind : LineKind) : Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
   109	  (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))).map fun k =>
   110	    (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k))
   111	
   112	/-- The mixing law of the sub-line lemma: the equal mixture over the two kinds
   113	of the law of the pair of source indices of a uniform extended coordinate.
   114	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   116	noncomputable def subLineComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   117	    Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
   118	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2))
   119	    ![subLineComponentBranch P .axis, subLineComponentBranch P .diagonal]
   120	
   121	/-- The mixing law has total mass one. -/
   122	theorem subLineComponentDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   123	    (subLineComponentDist P).IsProbability := by
   124	  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
   125	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun c _ => ?_
   126	  fin_cases c
   127	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   128	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _
   129	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   130	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _
   131	
   132	/-! ## The two projected marginals of one branch -/
   133	
   134	/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
   135	the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
   136	coordinate, of the `X` component laws.  Blueprint
   137	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   138	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   139	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
   140	    (kind : LineKind) :
   141	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineXProjection =
   142	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
   143	        (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
   144	  classical
   145	  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   146	    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
   147	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   148	  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at P kind k
   149	
   150	/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
   151	the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
   152	coordinate, of the `Z` component laws.  Blueprint
   153	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   154	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   155	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
   156	    (kind : LineKind) :
   157	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineZProjection =
   158	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
   159	        (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
   160	  classical
   161	  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   162	    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
   163	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   164	  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at P kind k
   165	
   166	/-! ## The two projected marginals of the sub-line law -/
   167	
   168	/-- The `X` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `X`
   169	component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
   170	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   172	theorem subLineDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   173	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineXProjection =
   174	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
   175	  classical
   176	  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   177	    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
   178	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   179	  fin_cases c
   180	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .axis
   181	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .diagonal
   182	
   183	/-- The `Z` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `Z`
   184	component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
   185	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   186	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   187	theorem subLineDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   188	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineZProjection =
   189	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
   190	  classical
   191	  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   192	    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
   193	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   194	  fin_cases c
   195	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .axis
   196	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .diagonal
   197	
   198	/-- The two one-point projected marginals of the sub-line law are mixtures of
   199	the restricted product laws along one common mixing law.  Blueprint
   200	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   201	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   202	theorem subLineDist_source_mixture (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   203	    ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
   204	      components.IsProbability ∧
   205	        (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineXProjection =
   206	          Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
   207	        (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineZProjection =
   208	          Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P) :=
   209	  ⟨subLineComponentDist P, subLineComponentDist_isProbability P,
   210	    subLineDist_map_subLineXProjection P,
   211	    subLineDist_map_subLineZProjection P⟩
   212	
   213	end
   214	
   215	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.SubLineBranch

     4	
     5	/-!
     6	# The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma
     7	
     8	This module carries out the sampling procedure of `lem:qld-sublines`.  A line
     9	kind is drawn from the two kinds, an extended coordinate and an extended point
    10	and direction are drawn uniformly, and two scalar seeds are drawn
    11	independently in the coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates that the
    12	two source lines must carry.  The sampled triple consists of the axis or
    13	diagonal line of the extended sample together with the two source lines
    14	decoded from the two coordinate blocks of the extended point and direction and
    15	from the two seeds.
    16	
    17	The module records the elementary evaluations of that triple, the description
    18	of the support of the resulting law, the three pointwise properties of a
    19	sampled triple -- incidence of the two source blocks, compatibility of the
    20	affine data, and closure of the axis branch -- and the identification of its
    21	extended-line marginal.
    22	
    23	## References
    24	
    25	The construction is the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    26	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    28	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    29	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    30	-/
    31	
    32	open scoped BigOperators
    33	
    34	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    35	
    36	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-! ## The auxiliary randomness of one branch -/
    41	
    42	/-- An extended point together with an extended direction.  Blueprint
    43	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    45	abbrev SubLinePointDir (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    46	  (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    47	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
    48	
    49	/-- The auxiliary randomness of one branch of the sampling procedure: an
    50	extended point, an extended direction, and the two scalar seeds of the two
    51	source lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	abbrev SubLineRaw (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    54	  SubLinePointDir P × (ScalarQ P.toLdParams × ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
    55	
    56	/-- The law of the scalar seed carried by a source line at a given coordinate
    57	index: uniform on the coordinate-index fiber of that index.  Blueprint
    58	`def:ith-restricted-line`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
    60	noncomputable def subLineSeedDist (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    61	    Distribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams) :=
    62	  Distribution.restrict (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ P.toLdParams))
    63	    (ldSeedIndexEvent P.toLdParams i) (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    64	
    65	/-- Every seed law of a source line has total mass one. -/
    66	theorem subLineSeedDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
    67	    (subLineSeedDist P i).IsProbability := by
    68	  rw [subLineSeedDist]
    69	  exact Distribution.restrict_isProbability _ _
    70	    (ldSeedIndexEvent_positive P.toLdParams i)
    71	
    72	/-- The auxiliary randomness law of the sampling procedure: the extended
    73	coordinate is uniform, the extended point and direction are uniform and
    74	independent of it, and the two seeds are independent and uniform on the
    75	coordinate-index fibers of the two coordinates carried by the two source
    76	lines.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    78	noncomputable def subLineRawDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    79	    Distribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLineRaw P) :=
    80	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
    81	    (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    82	        (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    83	          (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map fun w => (k, w)
    84	
    85	/-- The auxiliary randomness law has total mass one. -/
    86	theorem subLineRawDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (subLineRawDist P).IsProbability := by
    88	  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
    89	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun k _ => ?_
    90	  exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
    91	    (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability _)
    92	      (Distribution.prod_isProbability _ _ (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _)
    93	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P _))) _
    94	
    95	/-! ## The sampled triple -/
    96	
    97	/-- The extended line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line of an
    98	extended sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	noncomputable def subLineExtLineOfSample (P : AdmissibleParams)
   101	    (kind : LineKind) (s : DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd) :
   102	    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
   103	  match kind with
   104	  | .axis => directALineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   105	  | .diagonal => directDLineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   106	
   107	/-- The extended line of a branch, read off the auxiliary randomness.
   108	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   109	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   110	noncomputable def subLineExtLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   111	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   112	    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
   113	  subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩
   114	
   115	/-- A source line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line decoded
   116	from a point block, a scalar seed and a direction block.  Blueprint
   117	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   119	noncomputable def subLineSourceLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   120	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   121	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : LineDesc P.toLdParams :=
   122	  match kind with
   123	  | .axis => aLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   124	  | .diagonal => dLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   125	
   126	/-- The triple sampled by one branch of the procedure: the extended line
   127	together with the two source lines decoded from its two coordinate blocks and
   128	from the two scalar seeds.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`,

   218	  have hbind : sample ∈ (uniformDistribution (Fin 2)).support.biUnion
   219	      (fun c => (![subLineBranchDist P .axis,
   220	        subLineBranchDist P .diagonal] c).support) := hsample
   221	  obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hbind
   222	  obtain ⟨kind, hkind⟩ : ∃ kind : LineKind,
   223	      sample ∈ (subLineBranchDist P kind).support := by
   224	    fin_cases c
   225	    · exact ⟨.axis, by simpa using hc⟩
   226	    · exact ⟨.diagonal, by simpa using hc⟩
   227	  obtain ⟨kw, hkw, hkw'⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hkind
   228	  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp
   229	    (show kw ∈ (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))).support.biUnion

   233	        (fun w => (k, w))).support) from hkw)

   236	  obtain ⟨hsx, hsz⟩ := Finset.mem_product.mp hseeds

   238	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hsx).2
   239	  have hz : chiIndex P.toLdParams w.2.2 = subLineZIndex P k :=
   240	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hsz).2
   241	  refine ⟨kind, k, w, hx, hz, ?_⟩
   242	  rw [← hkw', ← hw']

item.text: The construction is not identical to the paper’s prose in its unused-index choices: it fixes those indices to the first coordinate instead of sampling them uniformly. That is not yet a defect in the theorem, because `lem:qld-sublines` only requires some mixture over restricted components, and the zero/noninherited blocks make those deterministic choices admissible. I’m checking the exact line encodings and canonical-representative lemmas to ensure this weaker sampling still proves every advertised field.

   340	  classical
   341	  have hfun : (fun z : LdSpace L =>
   342	        (aLineDescOfBlock L (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z),
   343	          (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z).1)) =
   344	      fun z : LdSpace L => (aLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z) := by
   345	    funext z
   346	    have h : (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z) = z :=
   347	      (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm_apply_apply z
   348	    show (aLineDescOf L ((ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z)),
   349	        LdSpace.point z) = (aLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z)
   350	    rw [h]
   351	  rw [restrictedALineDist_eq_map_restrict,
   352	    ← restrict_uniform_ldSeedEvent_map_block, Distribution.map_map, hfun]

   359	theorem restrictedDLineDist_eq_map_prod (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :

   361	      (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   362	          (freshDiagonalPairDist L i)).map
   363	        (fun w => (dLineDescOfBlock L w, w.1)) := by
   364	  classical
   365	  have hfun : (fun z : LdSpace L =>
   366	        (dLineDescOfBlock L (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z),
   367	          (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z).1)) =
   368	      fun z : LdSpace L => (dLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z) := by

   370	    have h : (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z) = z :=
   371	      (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm_apply_apply z
   372	    show (dLineDescOf L ((ldSpaceBlockEquiv L).symm (ldSpaceBlockEquiv L z)),
   373	        LdSpace.point z) = (dLineDescOf L z, LdSpace.point z)
   374	    rw [h]

   376	    ← restrict_uniform_ldSeedEvent_map_block, Distribution.map_map, hfun]

     3	/-!
     4	# The branch data of the sub-line sampling procedure
     5	
     6	The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma draws a line kind, a stored
     7	extended coordinate, and an unrestricted extended direction, and forms from
     8	them the direction of the extended line: the elementary direction at the
     9	stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with the
    10	coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the diagonal
    11	branch.  The two source lines are then read off the two coordinate blocks.
    12	This module fixes the coordinate index that each source line must carry: the
    13	stored coordinate itself when it belongs to that block, the first coordinate
    14	otherwise.  With that choice the source block of the extended direction always
    15	lies in the line spanned by the corresponding source direction, which is the
    16	incidence hypothesis of the two projection lemmas.  The module also records
    17	that moving an extended point to its canonical representative does not change
    18	the canonical representative of either of its source blocks.
    19	
    20	## References
    21	
    22	The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    23	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    25	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    26	445--480, paper lines 970--989; the prefix truncation is that of
    27	blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`.
    28	-/
    29	
    30	open scoped BigOperators
    31	
    32	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    33	
    34	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    35	
    36	noncomputable section
    37	
    38	/-! ## The three ranges of extended coordinates -/
    39	
    40	/-- Every extended coordinate is an `X`-block coordinate, a `Z`-block
    41	coordinate, or one of the two scalar coordinates.  Blueprint
    42	`def:combine-map`, paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    44	theorem extendedCoordinate_cases (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (2 * m + 2)) :
    45	    (∃ i : Fin m, k = embX m i) ∨ (∃ j : Fin m, k = embZ m j) ∨
    46	      k = alphaVar m ∨ k = betaVar m := by
    47	  rcases lt_or_ge k.val m with hk | hk
    48	  · exact Or.inl ⟨⟨k.val, hk⟩, Fin.ext (embX_val m ⟨k.val, hk⟩).symm⟩
    49	  · rcases lt_or_ge k.val (2 * m) with hk2 | hk2
    50	    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨⟨k.val - m, by omega⟩, Fin.ext ?_⟩)
    51	      rw [embZ_val]
    52	      change k.val = m + (k.val - m)
    53	      omega
    54	    · have hk3 : k.val < 2 * m + 2 := k.isLt
    55	      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge k.val (2 * m + 1) with hk4 | hk4
    56	      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl (Fin.ext ?_)))
    57	        rw [alphaVar_val]
    58	        omega
    59	      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Fin.ext ?_)))
    60	        rw [betaVar_val]
    61	        omega
    62	
    63	/-! ## Linearity of the identification of the two scalar fields -/
    64	
    65	/-- The identification of the two scalar fields is additive on extended
    66	points.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    68	theorem directPointToPauli_add (P : AdmissibleParams)
    69	    (u v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    70	    directPointToPauli P (u + v) =
    71	      directPointToPauli P u + directPointToPauli P v := by
    72	  funext i
    73	  simp [directPointToPauli]
    74	
    75	/-- The identification of the two scalar fields carries a scalar multiple of
    76	an extended point to the multiple by the identified scalar.  Blueprint
    77	`def:combine-map`, paper
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    79	theorem directPointToPauli_smul (P : AdmissibleParams)
    80	    (t : DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
    81	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    82	    directPointToPauli P (t • u) =
    83	      extendedDirectScalarEquiv P t • directPointToPauli P u := by
    84	  funext i
    85	  simp [directPointToPauli]
    86	
    87	/-! ## The coordinate index carried by each source line -/
    88	
    89	/-- The first coordinate of the source space.  Blueprint
    90	`eq:chi-func`, paper
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    92	-/
    93	def subLineFirstIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fin P.m :=
    94	  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.one_le_m⟩
    95	
    96	/-- The coordinate index carried by the source `X` line of a branch: the
    97	stored extended coordinate when it is an `X`-block coordinate, and the first
    98	coordinate otherwise.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	def subLineXIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) : Fin P.m :=
   101	  if h : k.val < P.m then ⟨k.val, h⟩ else subLineFirstIndex P
   102	
   103	/-- The coordinate index carried by the source `Z` line of a branch: the
   104	stored extended coordinate when it is a `Z`-block coordinate, and the first
   105	coordinate otherwise.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	def subLineZIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) : Fin P.m :=
   108	  if h : P.m ≤ k.val ∧ k.val < 2 * P.m then ⟨k.val - P.m, by omega⟩
   109	  else subLineFirstIndex P
   110	
   111	/-- At an `X`-block coordinate the source `X` line carries that coordinate. -/
   112	theorem subLineXIndex_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   113	    subLineXIndex P (embX P.m i) = i := by
   114	  have h : (embX P.m i).val < P.m := by
   115	    rw [embX_val]
   116	    exact i.isLt
   117	  rw [subLineXIndex, dif_pos h]
   118	  exact Fin.ext (embX_val P.m i)
   119	
   120	/-- At a `Z`-block coordinate the source `X` line carries the first
   121	coordinate. -/
   122	theorem subLineXIndex_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (j : Fin P.m) :
   123	    subLineXIndex P (embZ P.m j) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   124	  have h : ¬ (embZ P.m j).val < P.m := by
   125	    rw [embZ_val]
   126	    omega
   127	  rw [subLineXIndex, dif_neg h]
   128	
   129	/-- At the first scalar coordinate the source `X` line carries the first
   130	coordinate. -/
   131	theorem subLineXIndex_alphaVar (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   132	    subLineXIndex P (alphaVar P.m) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   133	  have h : ¬ (alphaVar P.m).val < P.m := by
   134	    rw [alphaVar_val]
   135	    omega
   136	  rw [subLineXIndex, dif_neg h]
   137	
   138	/-- At the second scalar coordinate the source `X` line carries the first
   139	coordinate. -/
   140	theorem subLineXIndex_betaVar (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   141	    subLineXIndex P (betaVar P.m) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   142	  have h : ¬ (betaVar P.m).val < P.m := by
   143	    rw [betaVar_val]
   144	    omega
   145	  rw [subLineXIndex, dif_neg h]
   146	
   147	/-- At an `X`-block coordinate the source `Z` line carries the first
   148	coordinate. -/
   149	theorem subLineZIndex_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m) :
   150	    subLineZIndex P (embX P.m i) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   151	  have h : ¬ (P.m ≤ (embX P.m i).val ∧ (embX P.m i).val < 2 * P.m) := by
   152	    rw [embX_val]
   153	    have := i.isLt
   154	    omega
   155	  rw [subLineZIndex, dif_neg h]
   156	
   157	/-- At a `Z`-block coordinate the source `Z` line carries that coordinate. -/
   158	theorem subLineZIndex_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (j : Fin P.m) :
   159	    subLineZIndex P (embZ P.m j) = j := by
   160	  have hj := j.isLt
   161	  have h : P.m ≤ (embZ P.m j).val ∧ (embZ P.m j).val < 2 * P.m := by
   162	    rw [embZ_val]
   163	    omega
   164	  rw [subLineZIndex, dif_pos h]
   165	  refine Fin.ext ?_
   166	  change (embZ P.m j).val - P.m = j.val
   167	  rw [embZ_val]
   168	  omega
   169	
   170	/-- At the first scalar coordinate the source `Z` line carries the first
   171	coordinate. -/
   172	theorem subLineZIndex_alphaVar (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   173	    subLineZIndex P (alphaVar P.m) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   174	  have h : ¬ (P.m ≤ (alphaVar P.m).val ∧ (alphaVar P.m).val < 2 * P.m) := by
   175	    rw [alphaVar_val]
   176	    omega
   177	  rw [subLineZIndex, dif_neg h]
   178	
   179	/-- At the second scalar coordinate the source `Z` line carries the first
   180	coordinate. -/
   181	theorem subLineZIndex_betaVar (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   182	    subLineZIndex P (betaVar P.m) = subLineFirstIndex P := by
   183	  have h : ¬ (P.m ≤ (betaVar P.m).val ∧ (betaVar P.m).val < 2 * P.m) := by
   184	    rw [betaVar_val]
   185	    omega
   186	  rw [subLineZIndex, dif_neg h]
   187	
   188	/-! ## The two directions of a branch -/
   189	
   190	/-- The direction of the extended line of a branch: the elementary direction
   191	at the stored coordinate in the axis branch, and the extended direction with
   192	the coordinates preceding the stored coordinate replaced by zero in the
   193	diagonal branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   194	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   195	def subLineExtDirection (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   196	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2))
   197	    (w : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   198	    Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd :=
   199	  match kind with
   200	  | .axis => coordinateDirection k
   201	  | .diagonal => directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) k w
   202	
   203	/-- The direction of a source line of a branch: the elementary direction at
   204	its coordinate index in the axis branch, and the given source block with the
   205	coordinates preceding that index replaced by zero in the diagonal branch.
   206	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   207	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   208	def subLineSourceDirection (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   209	    (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
   210	  match kind with
   211	  | .axis => coordinateDirection i
   212	  | .diagonal => prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i v

   214	/-! ## Incidence of the two source blocks of a branch direction -/
   215	
   216	/-- The `X` block of the direction of the extended line of a branch lies in
   217	the line spanned by the direction of its source `X` line.  Blueprint
   218	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   219	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   220	theorem projX_subLineExtDirection_mem_span (P : AdmissibleParams)
   221	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2))
   222	    (w : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   223	    projX (directPointToPauli P (subLineExtDirection P kind k w)) ∈
   224	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P)
   225	        ({subLineSourceDirection P kind (subLineXIndex P k)
   226	          (projX (directPointToPauli P w))} :
   227	          Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   228	  rcases extendedCoordinate_cases P.m k with ⟨i, rfl⟩ | ⟨j, rfl⟩ | rfl | rfl <;>
   229	    cases kind
   230	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   231	        (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) =
   232	        (coordinateDirection i : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) := by
   233	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   234	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_embX i
   235	    rw [subLineXIndex_embX]
   236	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   237	      (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) ∈ _
   238	    rw [hval]
   239	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   240	  · rw [subLineXIndex_embX]
   241	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   242	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) w)) ∈ _
   243	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_embX]
   244	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   245	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   246	        (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) = 0 := by
   247	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   248	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_embZ j
   249	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   250	      (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) ∈ _
   251	    rw [hval]
   252	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   253	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   254	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m j) w)) ∈ _
   255	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_embZ]
   256	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   257	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   258	        (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   259	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   260	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_alphaVar
   261	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   262	      (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   263	    rw [hval]
   264	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   265	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   266	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   267	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar]
   268	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   269	  · have hval : projX (directPointToPauli P
   270	        (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   271	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   272	      exact projX_coordinateDirection_betaVar
   273	    change projX (directPointToPauli P
   274	      (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   275	    rw [hval]
   276	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   277	  · change projX (directPointToPauli P
   278	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   279	    rw [projX_directPrefixProjection_betaVar]
   280	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   281

   283	the line spanned by the direction of its source `Z` line.  In the diagonal
   284	branch at an `X`-block coordinate the `Z` block is untruncated, which is why
   285	the source `Z` line carries the first coordinate there.  Blueprint
   286	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   287	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   288	theorem projZ_subLineExtDirection_mem_span (P : AdmissibleParams)
   289	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2))
   290	    (w : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   291	    projZ (directPointToPauli P (subLineExtDirection P kind k w)) ∈
   292	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P)
   293	        ({subLineSourceDirection P kind (subLineZIndex P k)
   294	          (projZ (directPointToPauli P w))} :
   295	          Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by

   297	    cases kind
   298	  · have hval : projZ (directPointToPauli P
   299	        (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) = 0 := by
   300	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   301	      exact projZ_coordinateDirection_embX i
   302	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   303	      (coordinateDirection (embX P.m i))) ∈ _
   304	    rw [hval]
   305	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   306	  · rw [subLineZIndex_embX]
   307	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   308	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) w)) ∈ _
   309	    rw [projZ_directPrefixProjection_embX]
   310	    change _ ∈ Submodule.span (PauliScalar P)
   311	      ({prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) (subLineFirstIndex P)
   312	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P w))} : Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   313	    rw [prefixProjection_of_val_zero (L := P.toLdParams)
   314	      (i := subLineFirstIndex P) rfl]
   315	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   316	  · have hval : projZ (directPointToPauli P
   317	        (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) =
   318	        (coordinateDirection j : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) := by
   319	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   320	      exact projZ_coordinateDirection_embZ j
   321	    rw [subLineZIndex_embZ]
   322	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   323	      (coordinateDirection (embZ P.m j))) ∈ _
   324	    rw [hval]
   325	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   326	  · rw [subLineZIndex_embZ]
   327	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   328	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m j) w)) ∈ _
   329	    rw [projZ_directPrefixProjection_embZ]
   330	    exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _
   331	  · have hval : projZ (directPointToPauli P
   332	        (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   333	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   334	      exact projZ_coordinateDirection_alphaVar
   335	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   336	      (coordinateDirection (alphaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   337	    rw [hval]
   338	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   339	  · change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   340	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   341	    rw [projZ_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar]
   342	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   343	  · have hval : projZ (directPointToPauli P
   344	        (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) = 0 := by
   345	      rw [directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection]
   346	      exact projZ_coordinateDirection_betaVar
   347	    change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   348	      (coordinateDirection (betaVar P.m))) ∈ _
   349	    rw [hval]
   350	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   351	  · change projZ (directPointToPauli P
   352	      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) w)) ∈ _
   353	    rw [projZ_directPrefixProjection_betaVar]
   354	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   355	
   356	/-! ## Canonical representatives of the two source blocks -/
   357	
   358	/-- Replacing an extended point by its canonical representative in the
   359	direction of the extended line does not change the canonical representative
   360	of its `X` block in the direction of the source `X` line, as soon as the `X`
   361	block of the extended direction lies in the line spanned by the source
   362	direction.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   363	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   364	theorem lineRepMap_projX_directPointToPauli_lineRepMap (P : AdmissibleParams)
   365	    (v x : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   366	    (dX : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   367	    (hdir : projX (directPointToPauli P v) ∈
   368	      Submodule.span (PauliScalar P) ({dX} : Set (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))) :
   369	    lineRepMap dX (projX (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x))) =
   370	      lineRepMap dX (projX (directPointToPauli P x)) := by
   371	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v x)
   372	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hdir
   373	  have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + t • v := by
   374	    rw [ht]
   375	    abel
   376	  have hstep : projX (directPointToPauli P x) =
   377	      projX (directPointToPauli P (lineRepMap v x)) +
   378	        (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P t * c) • dX := by
   379	    conv_lhs => rw [hx]

     3	/-!
     4	# Question and answer transport for the directly indexed low-degree game
     5	
     6	This module reads low individual degree test questions as canonical direct
     7	questions and rebases direct answers to the LDT line parametrization.
     8	
     9	Points and lines are decoded with the coordinate order reversed
    10	(`directPointEquiv`), so that the suffix-zero direction restriction of the
    11	LDT diagonal test becomes the prefix-zero restriction of the direct game.
    12	An LDT diagonal line reveals no coordinate index, whereas a direct diagonal
    13	question carries one.  The transported question uses the *leading index* of
    14	the decoded direction, the least coordinate at which the direction is
    15	nonzero.  Under the direct sampler, this is the index attached to the sampled
    16	direction exactly when the direction is nonzero at the sampled index
    17	(`directDiagonalIndexOf_prefixProjection`), an event of conditional
    18	probability `1 - 1/q`; on the LDT side, the leading index of a decoded
    19	`j`-restricted direction is `Fin.rev j` exactly when its pivot coordinate is
    20	nonzero (`directDiagonalIndexOf_extendRestrictedDirection`).  Diagonal answers
    21	on zero-direction lines are read as the constant polynomial carrying their
    22	value at the base point, following `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
    23	
    24	## References
    25	
    26	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:230-272`
    27	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:49-65`
    28	- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`
    29	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    30	-/

    35

    43	/-- A chosen affine parameter expressing a point relative to its canonical
    44	line representative. -/

    49	/-- The chosen canonical rebase parameter reconstructs the original point. -/
    50	theorem directLineRepParameter_spec
    51	    {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :

    56	direction. -/
