   458	/-- The index-first decomposition of an extended direct sample, read at the
   459	bare extended dimension.  This is the decomposition
   460	`directLdSpaceIndexEquiv` of `def:ld-question-distribution` with its stored
   461	coordinate typed by the bare dimension `2 m + 2`. -/
   462	private def subLineSampleEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   463	    DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd ≃
   464	      Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P where
   465	  toFun s := (s.index, s.point, s.direction)
   466	  invFun w := ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩
   467	  left_inv s := by cases s; rfl
   468	  right_inv w := by cases w; rfl
   469	
   470	/-- The extended-line marginal of one branch of the sub-line law is the law of
   471	the canonical line of the corresponding kind through a uniformly sampled
   472	extended direct sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   473	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   474	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_fst (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
   475	    (subLineBranchDist P kind).map Prod.fst =
   476	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   477	        (subLineExtLineOfSample P kind) := by
   478	  classical
   479	  have hstep1 : (subLineBranchDist P kind).map Prod.fst =
   480	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
   481	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   482	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   483	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
   484	          fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩ := by
   485	    rw [subLineBranchDist, Distribution.map_map, subLineRawDist,
   486	      Distribution.bind_map]
   487	    refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   488	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   489	    rfl
   490	  have hstep2 : ∀ k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2),
   491	      (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   492	          (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   493	            (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
   494	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩) =
   495	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P)).map
   496	        (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩) := by
   497	    intro k
   498	    exact Distribution.prod_map_of_fst
   499	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   500	      (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   501	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))
   502	      (Distribution.prod_isProbability
   503	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   504	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k))
   505	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P (subLineXIndex P k))
   506	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P (subLineZIndex P k)))
   507	      (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩)
   508	  have hstep3 :
   509	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) (fun k =>
   510	        (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P)).map
   511	          (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩)) =
   512	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P)).map
   513	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩) := by
   514	    rw [uniformDistribution_prod (Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (SubLinePointDir P)]
   515	    exact (Distribution.prod_map_eq_bind
   516	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2)))
   517	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   518	      (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩)).symm
   519	  have hstep4 :
   520	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P)).map
   521	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩) =
   522	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   523	        (subLineExtLineOfSample P kind) := by
   524	    rw [← uniformDistribution_map_equiv (subLineSampleEquiv P),
   525	      Distribution.map_map]
   526	    rfl
   527	  rw [hstep1, Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ (fun k _ => hstep2 k),
   528	    hstep3, hstep4]
   529	
   530	/-- The extended-line marginal of the sub-line law is the extended-line
   531	marginal of the directly indexed line-point law.  Blueprint
   532	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   533	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   534	theorem subLineDist_map_fst (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   535	    (subLineDist P).map Prod.fst =
   536	      (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   537	  classical
   538	  have haxis : (subLineBranchDist P .axis).map Prod.fst =
   539	      (directALinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   540	    rw [subLineBranchDist_map_fst, directALinePointDist, Distribution.map_map]
   541	    rfl
   542	  have hdiag : (subLineBranchDist P .diagonal).map Prod.fst =
   543	      (directDLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   544	    rw [subLineBranchDist_map_fst, directDLinePointDist, Distribution.map_map]
   545	    rfl
   546	  rw [subLineDist, Distribution.bind_map, directLinePointDist,
   547	    ← Distribution.bind_uniform_fin_two, Distribution.bind_map]
   548	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   549	  fin_cases c
   550	  · exact haxis
   551	  · exact hdiag
   552

    37	/-! ## The canonical representative for the zero direction -/
    38	
    39	/-- For the zero direction the canonical representative map of
    40	`def:line-representative` is the identity, since the span of the zero vector
    41	is trivial.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`, paper
    42	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    43	-/
    44	theorem lineRepMap_zero_apply {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    45	    (u : Fin m → K) : lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) u = u := by
    46	  have hspan : Submodule.span K ({0} : Set (Fin m → K)) = ⊥ := by simp
    47	  have h := sub_lineRepMap_mem_span (0 : Fin m → K) u
    48	  rw [hspan, Submodule.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at h
    49	  exact h.symm
    50	
    51	/-! ## Uniform points of a line -/
    52	
    53	/-- The point at a uniformly random affine parameter on the line through the
    54	canonical representative of a uniformly random point is uniformly random on
    55	the whole coordinate space.  Every fiber of the parameterization has exactly
    56	`q` elements: for a nonzero direction the parameter is determined and the
    57	representative varies over a coset of the span of the direction, and for the
    58	zero direction the representative is the point itself and the parameter is
    59	free.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    61	theorem uniformDistribution_map_lineRepMap_add_smul {K : Type*} [Field K]
    62	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) :
    63	    (uniformDistribution ((Fin m → K) × K)).map
    64	        (fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v) =
    65	      uniformDistribution (Fin m → K) := by
    66	  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card K) fun x => ?_
    67	  by_cases hv : v = 0
    68	  · subst hv
    69	    have hfilter :
    70	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    71	            fun w => lineRepMap (0 : Fin m → K) w.1 + w.2 • (0 : Fin m → K)
    72	              = x)
    73	          = ({x} : Finset (Fin m → K)) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset K) := by
    74	      ext w
    75	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
    76	        Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_singleton, and_true, smul_zero,
    77	        add_zero, lineRepMap_zero_apply]
    78	    rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
    79	    simp
    80	  · have hinj : Function.Injective
    81	        (fun c : K => (lineRepMap v x + c • v, directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    82	      intro c₁ c₂ hc
    83	      have hc' : c₁ • v = c₂ • v := by
    84	        have h := congrArg Prod.fst hc
    85	        simpa using h
    86	      have hsub : (c₁ - c₂) • v = 0 := by
    87	        rw [sub_smul, hc', sub_self]
    88	      rcases smul_eq_zero.mp hsub with h | h
    89	      · exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
    90	      · exact absurd h hv
    91	    have himg :
    92	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin m → K) × K)).filter
    93	            fun w => lineRepMap v w.1 + w.2 • v = x)
    94	          = (Finset.univ : Finset K).image
    95	              (fun c => (lineRepMap v x + c • v,
    96	                directLineRepParameter v x)) := by
    97	      ext w
    98	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_image]
    99	      constructor
   100	      · intro hw
   101	        have hrep : lineRepMap v w.1 = lineRepMap v x := by
   102	          rw [← hw, lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   103	        have hx : x = lineRepMap v x + w.2 • v := by
   104	          rw [← hrep]
   105	          exact hw.symm
   106	        have ht : directLineRepParameter v x = w.2 :=
   107	          directLineRepParameter_eq_of_nonzero hv hx
   108	        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp
   109	          (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v w.1)
   110	        refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   111	        have hw1 : lineRepMap v x + c • v = w.1 := by
   112	          rw [← hrep, hc]
   113	          abel
   114	        rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   115	        exact ⟨hw1, ht⟩
   116	      · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
   117	        show lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v x + c • v) +
   118	          directLineRepParameter v x • v = x
   119	        rw [lineRepMap_add_smul, lineRepMap_apply_self]
   120	        exact (directLineRepParameter_spec v x).symm
   121	    rw [himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hinj, Finset.card_univ]

   128	theorem embX_injective (m : ℕ) : Function.Injective (embX m) := by

    35	
    36	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the

    38	`def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	noncomputable def directBlockToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    41	    (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃ (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) where
    42	  toFun v := fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v i)
    43	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    44	  left_inv v := by
    45	    funext i
    46	    simp
    47	  right_inv v := by
    48	    funext i
    49	    simp

    52	source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
    53	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    55	noncomputable def directPointToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :

    58	  toFun := directPointToPauli P
    59	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    60	  left_inv v := by
    61	    funext i
    62	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    63	  right_inv v := by
    64	    funext i
    65	    simp [directPointToPauli]

    68	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

    71	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    72	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projX u) := rfl

    74	/-- The `Z` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `Z`
    75	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

    81	/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
    82	
    83	/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field

    85	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    86	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (uniformDistribution
    88	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    89	        (directPointToPauli P) =
    90	      uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) :=
    91	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directPointToPauliEquiv P)
    92	
    93	/-- A uniformly random source block transported to the source scalar field is
    94	uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    96	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directBlockToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    97	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    98	        (fun v => directBlockToPauliEquiv P v) =
    99	      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :=
   100	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)

   102	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly random extended point, read in the
   103	source scalar field, are independent and uniformly random.  Blueprint
   104	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   106	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   107	    (uniformDistribution
   108	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   109	        (fun u => (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   110	          projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =

   115	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   116	          (projX (directPointToPauli P u), projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =

   139	    ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun w : (Fin m → K) × K =>

   107	theorem uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg

/-!
# Product rules for finite-support distribution averages

This module contains product and marginalization rules for operator-valued
uniform averages.  The scalar product rules, together with the common
PMF-weighted finite-sum identities on which both scalar and operator rules
depend, are in `MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionUniformSums` and
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.PMFAverages`.

## Main definitions / statements

* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_prod`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_comm`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_prod_swap`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_fst`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_snd`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_prod`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_prod_swap`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_fst`
* `averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_snd`

## References

These are formalization-internal finite probability lemmas for the low
individual degree test development.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Split a uniform operator average over a product into iterated uniform
operator averages. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_prod
    {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (f : α → β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (α × β))
        (fun ab => f ab.1 ab.2) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
        (fun a => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β)
          (fun b => f a b)) := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_prod (f := f)

/-- Swap two nested uniform operator averages over finite nonempty types. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_comm
    {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (f : α → β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
        (fun a => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β) (f a)) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β)
        (fun b => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
          (fun a => f a b)) := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_comm (f := f)

/-- Split a uniform operator average over a product into iterated uniform
operator averages, with the second coordinate averaged first. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_prod_swap
    {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (f : α → β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (α × β))
        (fun ab => f ab.1 ab.2) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β)
        (fun b => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
          (fun a => f a b)) := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_prod_swap (f := f)

/-- Operator averaging of a family depending only on the first coordinate
marginalizes a uniform product. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_fst
    {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (α × β)) (fun ab => f ab.1) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α) f := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_fst
      (e := Equiv.refl (α × β)) (f := f)

/-- Operator averaging of a family depending only on the second coordinate
marginalizes a uniform product. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_snd
    {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (f : β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (α × β)) (fun ab => f ab.2) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β) f := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_snd
      (e := Equiv.refl (α × β)) (f := f)

/-- Transport a uniform operator average through an equivalence whose target is
a product, then split the product average into iterated uniform averages. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_prod
    {γ α β : Type*}
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Nonempty γ]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (e : γ ≃ α × β) (f : γ → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution γ) f =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
        (fun a => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β)
          (fun b => f (e.symm (a, b)))) := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_prod (e := e) (f := f)

/-- Transport a uniform operator average through an equivalence whose target is
a product, then split the product average with the second coordinate averaged
first. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_prod_swap
    {γ α β : Type*}
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Nonempty γ]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (e : γ ≃ α × β) (f : γ → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution γ) f =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β)
        (fun b => averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α)
          (fun a => f (e.symm (a, b)))) := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_prod_swap (e := e) (f := f)

/-- A function depending only on the first coordinate of a product equivalence
has the corresponding first-coordinate uniform operator marginal. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_fst
    {γ α β : Type*}
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Nonempty γ]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Finite β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (e : γ ≃ α × β) (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution γ) (fun x => f (e x).1) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution α) f := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_fst (e := e) (f := f)

/-- A function depending only on the second coordinate of a product equivalence
has the corresponding second-coordinate uniform operator marginal. -/
theorem averageOperatorOverDistribution_uniform_equiv_snd
    {γ α β : Type*}
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Nonempty γ]
    [Finite α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (e : γ ≃ α × β) (f : β → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
    averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution γ) (fun x => f (e x).2) =
      averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution β) f := by
  simpa [averageOperatorOverDistribution] using
    uniformDistribution_sum_smul_equiv_snd (e := e) (f := f)

end MIPStarRE.LDT

    62	\section{Key theorem forms}
    63	
    64	Throughout, $q = 2^r$ with $r$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    65	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    66	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    67	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    68	theorem forms.
    69	\begin{enumerate}
    70	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    71	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    72	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    73	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    74	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    75	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    76	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    77	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    78	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    79	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    80	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    81	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    82	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    83	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    84	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    85	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    86	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    87	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    88	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    89	  \item \textbf{Divisibility-restricted source candidate.}  The source theorem
    90	  form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    91	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    92	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    93	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.  This restriction makes the auxiliary source game defined;
    94	  it does not settle either soundness-import obligation, so this form is not
    95	  established by the present route.
    96	  \item \textbf{Established directly indexed form.}  Quantum
    97	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    98	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    99	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
   100	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
   101	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
   102	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in

   136	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   137	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   138	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   139	individual degree game with parameters
   140	\[
   141	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   142	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   143	\]
   144	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   145	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   146	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution

   148	
   149	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   150	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   151	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   152	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   153	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   154	$\chi(s)$ with
   155	\[
   156	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   157	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   158	\]
   159	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   160	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   161	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   162	
   163	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   164	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   165	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   166	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   167	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   168	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   169	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   170	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility.  Thus even before the
   171	two soundness-import obligations below are considered, this route can apply to
   172	the polynomial-pair lemma only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

   174	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   175	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   176	
   177	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   178	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   179	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   180	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   181	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   182	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   183	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   184	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   185	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   186	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   187	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   188	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   189	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   190	open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
   191	the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
   192	where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
   193	soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
   194	established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
   195	the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.
   196	
   197	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   198	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   199	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   200	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   201	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   202	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   203	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   204	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   205	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   206	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   207	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   208	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   209	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   210	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   211	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   212	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   213	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   214	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   215	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   216	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   217	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   218	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   219	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   220	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   221	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   222	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   223	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   224	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   225	
   226	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   227	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   228	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   229	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   230	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   231	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   232	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   233	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   234	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   235	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   236	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   237	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   238	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   239	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   240	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   241	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   242	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   243	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   244	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
   245	only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   246	$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this
   247	dependence is now retained in a correlated residue register rather than
   248	averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of
   249	the direct-game transport, but it has not been composed with the distinct
   250	pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.
   251	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   252	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   253	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   254	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   255	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   256	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   257	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   258	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   259	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   260	which the test has no counterpart branch.

    33	/-! ## Restriction of a push-forward -/
    34	
    35	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restricting a push-forward distribution to a
    36	decidable event is the push-forward of the restriction to the pre-image of
    37	that event.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem Distribution.restrict_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (f : α → β) (p : β → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    41	    (q : α → Prop) [DecidablePred q] (hq : ∀ a, q a ↔ p (f a))
    42	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b)
    43	    (hpos' : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a) :
    44	    Distribution.restrict (μ.map f) p hpos =
    45	      (Distribution.restrict μ q hpos').map f := by
    46	  classical
    47	  have hfiber : ∀ b : β, p b →
    48	      μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    49	        (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b) := by
    50	    intro b hb
    51	    ext a
    52	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    53	    constructor
    54	    · rintro ⟨ha, hab⟩
    55	      exact ⟨⟨ha, (hq a).mpr (hab ▸ hb)⟩, hab⟩
    56	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha, -⟩, hab⟩
    57	      exact ⟨ha, hab⟩
    58	  have himg : (μ.map f).support.filter p = (μ.support.filter q).image f := by
    59	    ext b
    60	    simp only [Distribution.map_support, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_image]
    61	    constructor
    62	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hpb⟩
    63	      exact ⟨a, ⟨ha, (hq a).mpr hpb⟩, rfl⟩
    64	    · rintro ⟨a, ⟨ha1, ha2⟩, rfl⟩
    65	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha1, rfl⟩, (hq a).mp ha2⟩
    66	  have hmass : (∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b) =
    67	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a := by
    68	    rw [himg]
    69	    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    70	      (s := μ.support.filter q) (t := (μ.support.filter q).image f)
    71	      (g := f) (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image_of_mem f ha) μ.weight]
    72	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
    73	    obtain ⟨a0, ha0, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hb
    74	    rw [Distribution.map_weight,
    75	      hfiber _ ((hq a0).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha0).2)]
    76	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    77	  · exact himg
    78	  · funext b
    79	    show (if p b then (μ.map f).weight b /
    80	        ∑ c ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight c else 0) =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b),
    82	        (if q a then μ.weight a / ∑ c ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight c else 0)
    83	    by_cases hb : p b
    84	    · rw [if_pos hb, hmass, Distribution.map_weight, hfiber b hb,
    85	        Finset.sum_div]
    86	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    87	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1).2]
    88	    · rw [if_neg hb]
    89	      refine (Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha => ?_).symm
    90	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
    91	      exact absurd (ha2 ▸ (hq a).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha1).2) hb

/-!
# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions

This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.

## References

The combining map is blueprint
`def:combine-map`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
The restricted laws are blueprint `def:ith-restricted-line`,
with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

noncomputable section

/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)

/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Defs
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Consistency

/-!
# Witnesses for combining the Pauli bases

This module defines the five measurement and distribution witnesses used in
the combining argument.  Every measurement is indexed by the player side, so
Alice's and Bob's local spaces remain distinct.  The extended-dimensional
line objects use the directly indexed low-degree interface and therefore do
not require a dimension-divisibility hypothesis.

## References

`CombinedPointsWitness`, `CombinedLinesWitness`, and `GlobalPairWitness` record
the measurement conclusions of `lem:qld-4-10`, `lem:qld-xz-lines`, and
`lem:qld-4-7`, respectively, in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`.  `SubLineWitness` and
`ExtendedLinesWitness` instead support `lem:qld-sublines` and `lem:qld-4-13`
through the directly indexed extended-line carrier and probability law.  The
latter also uses the completed answer alphabet, rather than the field-valued
answer sum in the source statement.  The paper source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:689-709,
882-894,1020-1069,1267-1274`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-! ## The canonical scalar identification -/

/-- Identify the direct extended game's scalar field with the Pauli scalar
field.  Both are selected by `fixedFieldModel`; only their proof argument for
admissibility differs. -/
noncomputable def extendedDirectScalarEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd ≃+* PauliScalar P := by
  have h : P.extendedDirectLd.hq = P.hq := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  cases h
  exact RingEquiv.refl _

+
+The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
+elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
+distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
+game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
+linear distributions rely on.

+
+/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
+weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
+`Distribution`. -/
+theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
+    μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl
+
+/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
+theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
+    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
+    rw [Finset.image_image]
+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
+        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
+      intro a ha
+      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
+    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
+    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
+        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
+      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a

+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
+    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    congr 1

+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
+    constructor

+      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩

+    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
+  simp [uniformDistribution]

+/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
+distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
+    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
+    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
+  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
+    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
+    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
+      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
+    rwa [hc] at hpos
+  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
+    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
+      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
+      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
+    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
+    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
+    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]

+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]

+    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
+    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'

+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_

+/-- The second marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.

+theorem uniformDistribution_map_snd {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card α) fun b => ?_

+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp

+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
+theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (g : α → β → γ) :

+      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_

+    simp [Prod.exists]
+  · funext c
+    have hcount :

+      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
+              (1 / (Fintype.card β : Error)) := by
+      intro a
+      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,
+          (uniformDistribution β).weight b) = _
+      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,

+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c

+      intro a

+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c) =

+      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]

Honest axis- and diagonal-line measurements as coarse-grainings of the
generalized Pauli basis measurement by the degree-restricted encoding on the
canonical line of the question, using the line-degree bounds of
lem:pauli-completeness.  The pointwise Magic Square measurement at a question

observables, with projectivity, incident commutation and symmetry of effects.

single measurement family on all Pauli question types, acting on the Pauli
register tensored with the Magic Square qubit, and proves that family
projective with symmetric effects.

Export the Magic Square perfect-strategy helpers that the assembly reuses
instead of duplicating them (issue #204).

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/SubLineBind.lean:37` — Move the new generic finite-distribution laws into the shared distribution API instead of exposing them from sub-line feature modules.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/RestrictedMixture.lean:148` — Export and reuse the existing seed-marginal theorem instead of adding an acknowledged duplicate proof.

## Review

F1 covers a broad family of public, domain-independent results spread across `RestrictedMixture`, `RestrictedAverage`, `SubLineBind`, `SubLineBlocks`, `SubLineProduct`, `SubLineSeed`, `SubLineShuffle`, and `SubLineSupport`. Examples include `Distribution.bind_map_left`, `bind_bind`, `bind_const`, `prod_bind_left`, `restrict_prod_snd`, and `uniformDistribution_prod`. These belong in the existing shared distribution layer, such as `QPBT/Games/DistributionAux.lean` or an imported sibling. Keeping them here makes generic consumers depend on the sub-line implementation and fragments API ownership. This must be fixed before merge.

F2's docstring explicitly identifies `uniformDistribution_map_ldSeed` as a copy of the private `map_uniformDistribution_seed`. `Combining/Defs.lean` already imports `Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`, so there is no dependency-cycle justification for duplicating the proof. Promote or relocate the original theorem and reuse it in both callers. Tracking issue #204 documents the duplication but does not make this avoidable copy acceptable.

The mathematical statements were checked against `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1116` and blueprint labels `lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds` and `lem:qld-sublines`. The mixture weights, `2m` and `4m²` inflation factors, consistency bound, and quantifier order agree with the cited material. `exists_subLineWitness` remains explicitly scoped to the directly indexed auxiliary carrier and is not advertised as completing the unresolved source-dimensional statement.

The prior findings concerning the duplicate product-average lemma and `reindexOp_nonneg` were addressed. The relevant Lean files type-check, `git diff --check` passes, and no new proof holes or integrity bypasses were introduced. The two pre-existing combined-line `sorry`s remain the issue-#18 construction debt identified by the surrounding documentation.
